    Records and ViewSpec check a tree when it is built and throw IllegalArgumentException naming the problem; the kit checks icon names when a view is created or updated. A tree is refused when:

    • an id or a required label is blank, or a button without a label lacks an icon or a tooltip;
    • two nodes share an id (item, option, crumb, column and row ids need only be unique within their node, tree item ids within their tree), or two Custom nodes share a content id;
    • it is deeper than 128 levels or has more than 100,000 nodes;
    • a selected or expanded id names no item, a choice's selected id is not one of its options, an expanded id is not a tree branch, or a table cell names no column;
    • an EXCLUSIVE choice does not have two to four options, or a TABS choice fewer than two;
    • a field's list id names no ItemList in the same view;
    • a Notice stands outside a form's sections or a VERTICAL stack, or a Separator outside an INLINE or ACTIONS stack, first, last or beside another separator;
    • it names an icon that is neither built in nor registered by the plugin ("Unknown icon: name").

    Each record's own rules, such as which presentations a field kind takes, are in its entry in the API reference.

    Icons

    Icons are names. Jasper's built-in names are add, appearance, application, arrow.right, back, bell, bookmark, brightness, check, chevron.down, chevron.left, chevron.right, chevron.up, clock, close, collapse, collapse.all, command-palette, copy, cursor, delete, desktop, download, edit, editor.preview, editor.preview.classic, editor.scroll-sync, editor.scroll-sync.classic, editor.source, editor.source.classic, editor.split, editor.split.classic, error, expand.all, file, folder, folder.add, folder.filled, font, forward, help, hidden, history, home, import, info, key, keyboard, laptop, link, lock, lock.keyhole, login, logout, match.case, match.word, menu, more, more.vertical, network, none, note, notification.card, notification.history, notification.off, notification.sticky, paste, pause, play, play.filled, plugin, preview, question, refresh, regex, remove, reset, reveal, run, save, search, server, settings, shield, sparkle, split, star, star.filled, target, terminal, triangle.down, tunnel, unlock, upload, user, warning, window, window.add and zoom. They follow the theme and the look. run, IntelliJ's classic Run triangle, and application, its run-configuration icon, are authored artwork: controls draw them in their own colours, and panels, prompts and tiles draw a monochrome glyph of the same name. These two names need SDK 0.18.1. editor.source, editor.split, editor.preview and editor.scroll-sync are a document's view controls (source only, source and preview, preview only, synchronised scrolling) in IntelliJ's New UI art, and their .classic names are IntelliJ's classic art, for use while Presentation.icons() is Presentation.Icons.CLASSIC. All eight are authored light and dark art that Jasper draws in its own colours wherever the name appears; they need SDK 0.18.3. Under the Enterprise look a tool window's stripe label starts with its icon, and IntelliJ's classic art draws network, folder, tunnel, download, server and bell there, and add, split, zoom, settings, window.add and search in the toolbar, toolbar views, the status bar and tool-window headers; view bodies keep the ordinary art.

    A plugin adds its own with UiKit.registerIcon(IconAsset). An IconAsset's name is <plugin id>:<name>, the name a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits, dots and dashes; its artwork is SVG path data on a 16-unit grid, starting with a move and using only the M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A and Z commands, at most 8,192 characters and 2,048 commands, with at least one drawn segment. Jasper strokes it as an outline in its own colour, size and stroke width, so it matches the built-in icons. Register icons in start, before anything names them:

    context.kit().registerIcon(new IconAsset("dev.example.tool:rocket",
    "M 8 1.5 C 10.5 3 11.5 5.5 11.5 8.5 L 9.5 11 H 6.5 L 4.5 8.5 C 4.5 5.5 5.5 3 8 1.5 Z M 6.5 11 L 5.5 14.5 M 9.5 11 L 10.5 14.5"));

    Action, panel, status item, toolbar menu, palette and content tab icons take the same names. The plugin's own identity icon is a file in its jar, named by the manifest's icon key. See plugin icons.

    Custom content

    For what descriptors cannot express, such as a text editor, a chart or a preview, a tree holds a Nodes.Custom node and the plugin registers a component for it with UiView.registerContent(CustomContent). The CustomContent's id and kind (EDITOR, TERMINAL, CHART or PREVIEW) match the node's; its lifetime closes when the node leaves the tree or the view closes. Jasper admits a purpose-built canvas, a JComponent that is not a panel, label, button, list, table, tree, combo box, spinner, slider or text component (a JScrollPane is judged by what it scrolls); an EDITOR may also be a JTextArea, JTextPane or JEditorPane. Anything else is refused ("Ordinary plugin controls require kit descriptors"). Jasper sets the component's foreground and background from the theme whenever the theme changes, with the workspace's opacity in a translucent window, and its font to the interface's body font when it is registered, at every update of the view and at every theme or font change, so a font of the plugin's own belongs on a component inside it; the component paints the rest from Appearance.

    Colours

    Views take their colours from the theme without help. Custom content reads them from PluginContext.appearance(): Appearance.color(SemanticColor) for one of the theme's semantic colours, Appearance.workspacePalette(), Appearance.editorPalette() and Appearance.syntaxPalette() for the workspace, where terminals and content tabs live, and Appearance.workspaceOpacity(Component) for the alpha of a translucent workspace. Read them on the UI thread, and again after Appearance.onChanged(Consumer) or Appearance.onWorkspaceChanged(Consumer): the user can change the theme, and the chrome and the workspace can follow different themes. On the event bus, AppEvents.THEME_CHANGED announces each change of the chrome's theme or the interface font.

    The look

    Views follow the look without help too. A plugin that composes differently under a look, or custom content that needs the look's faces, reads Appearance.presentation(): a Presentation that says whether the look starts from the classic catalog, its icon set, whether tool windows are reached by icon rails or labelled stripes, the title bar and where the menus are on this platform, whether the toolbar offers Search Everywhere as a field or an icon, the look's UI and data faces (empty for the platform's), its body text size and its default toolbar height. Jasper chooses the look at start, so the value is the same for every plugin until it restarts, and it is safe from any thread: read it once in start. It reports the look's own faces, sizes, title bar and menus, not the user's interface font, toolbar height, decoration or view settings. Remote, Credential Vault and File Server compose their classic layouts when Presentation.classic() is true, and the Sample starts its tool window in the bottom strip under labelled stripes:

    boolean classic = context.appearance().presentation().classic();
Anchor side = context.appearance().presentation().toolWindows() == Presentation.ToolWindows.STRIPES ? Anchor.BOTTOM : Anchor.LEFT;

    Appearance.presentation() needs SDK 0.18.2. In a test, FakePluginHost.setPresentation(Presentation) with FakePresentations.CLASSIC runs the plugin under the Enterprise look's values.

    The terminal font

    Custom content that shows text in the terminal's font, as the Editor does when it follows the terminal font, reads Appearance.terminalTypography() and applies it to a component inside its registered content: a TerminalTypography with the saved family, the size in points (6 to 72, fractions allowed), the fallback families in the order they are tried, whether ligatures are on and the line height (a multiple from 0.5 to 3), as Settings › Terminal › Font & Colors saves them. The value is the same for every window and plugin, a pane's temporary zoom does not change it, and it is safe from any thread. Register Appearance.onTerminalTypographyChanged(Consumer) on the UI thread: the handler runs there after each saved change, when the getter already returns the new value. An equal value notifies nobody and registering delivers no initial value, so read the getter first; the registration closes with the plugin. Both need SDK 0.18.3. In a test, FakePluginHost.setTerminalTypography(TerminalTypography) publishes a value on the next flush().

    Settings

    A plugin's settings live in its own TOML file, plugins/<id>/<id>.toml in Jasper home, not in config.toml. The plugin declares each setting while it starts: its key, kind, default and how Settings shows it. Jasper then reads the file, checks every value against its kind, reports what it rejects, reads the file again whenever it changes, and gives the plugin a page in Settings › Tools under its name. PluginContext.settings() is the plugin's PluginSettings.

    Declaring

    PluginSettings settings = context.settings();
Setting<Integer> parallel = settings.declare(SettingSpec.of("transfers.parallel", SettingKind.integer(1, 16), 4)
    .label("Parallel transfers").description("Files copied at the same time.").section("Transfers"));
Setting<String> target = settings.declare(SettingSpec.of("target", SettingKind.choice(List.of(
        Choice.of("staging", "Staging", "staging"), Choice.of("production", "Production", "production"))), "staging")
    .label("Deploy target").section("Deploys"));
Setting<List<String>> checks = settings.declare(SettingSpec.of("checks", SettingKind.stringList(), List.of("lint", "test"))
    .label("Checks to run").section("Deploys").applies(Applies.RESTART));
parallel.onChanged(value -> context.log().log(System.Logger.Level.INFO, "Parallel transfers: " + value));

    The file the user edits, or Settings writes:

    target = "production"
checks = ["lint", "test", "smoke"]

[transfers]
parallel = 8

    PluginSettings.declare(SettingSpec) works only on the UI thread while start runs, and returns a Setting that already holds the file's value. A declaration needs a label; a key declared twice, or a key inside another declared key, is refused. Keys are dotted: each part is letters, digits, _ and -, and each dot but the last names a TOML table. Do not change a SettingSpec after declaring it: Settings reads its section, description, editor hint and unit again whenever it shows the page. Its builder methods are:

    MethodSettings shows
    SettingSpec.label(String)The row's name. Required.
    SettingSpec.description(String)A note under the control.
    SettingSpec.keywords(String[])Extra words Settings' search matches.
    SettingSpec.section(String)A heading on the plugin's page; a new heading starts wherever the section changes, in declaration order.
    SettingSpec.applies(Applies)Applies.RESTART marks the row "Takes effect after restart". It changes only the label: the value and its listeners still change at once, and a plugin that reads the value only in start picks it up at the next launch.
    SettingSpec.editor(EditorHint)EditorHint.font(boolean): a font family picker, monospaced families only when asked. EditorHint.file(): a path field with Browse ("Choose a file"). EditorHint.technical(): a text field in the data face, for hosts, ports, paths and commands. EditorHint.directory() shows the kind's own control.
    SettingSpec.unit(String)A unit after a number, such as min or MiB, at most 16 characters.

    Kinds

    KindValueIn the fileOn the pageJasper reports a rejected value as
    SettingKind.bool()Booleantrue or falseA switch or check box, as the look draws it
    SettingKind.integer(int, int)IntegerAn integerA stepper with the unit"Use an integer from min–max; using the default."
    SettingKind.number(double, double)DoubleA finite numberA decimal field that steps by 0.1, with the unit"Use a finite number from min–max; using the default."
    SettingKind.text(), SettingKind.text(Predicate, String)StringA stringA text fieldThe kind's message, "Not an allowed value." for text()
    SettingKind.choice(List)The Choice's valueThe choice's tokenA picker of the choices' display names"Use tokens; using the default.", the tokens sorted and separated by commas
    SettingKind.stringList(), SettingKind.stringList(Predicate)List<String>An array of stringsAn ordered list, with a field that adds an entry"Invalid string array element; using the default list."

    A text rule is plugin code: one that throws rejects the value. A default the kind rejects throws when the spec is built. Within Jasper a number setting's value is kept in single precision, so 0.1 reads back as 0.10000000149011612; round it where that matters.

    Reading the file

    Jasper checks the file once a second and reads it again when it changed; Reload Config reads every plugin's file again and then publishes AppEvents.CONFIG_RELOADED. Problems appear with Jasper's other configuration problems, naming the file and, for a value, its line and column:

    • A value its kind rejects is replaced by the setting's default and reported as the table above shows.
    • A key nothing declares is reported as "Unknown setting or table; ignored."
    • A value of the wrong TOML type, such as a string where an integer belongs, rejects the whole file ("Expected type; configuration was not applied."), and so does a TOML syntax error, a file larger than 1 MiB or one that cannot be read ("file could not be read: why; the last good settings stay in force."). Every setting keeps its last good value until the file is fixed.

    Setting.get() is the value in force, safe from any thread. Setting.onChanged(Consumer) runs on the UI thread when that setting's value changes, whether the file changed or the plugin saved it; PluginSettings.onChanged(Runnable) runs once after any declared value changed. The runtime closes these registrations when the plugin stops.

    When the file is missing, the first launch that finds the plugin creates it: a copy of the settings.toml at the root of the plugin's jar, or a one-line header, "# Settings for name version (id). Jasper reads this file live." Jasper never overwrites an existing file. Ship a settings.toml of commented examples so users who open the file see every setting.

    The look's defaults

    The active look's kit file may hold a table for the plugin, [defaults."<plugin id>"], keyed as the plugin's settings file writes its keys. When the plugin declares a key and the value suits its kind, that value is the setting's default while the look is active: a key the file leaves out reads it, and Reset returns to it, while a saved value still wins. A value the kind rejects, and a key the plugin does not declare, are logged as warnings and ignored, and the plugin starts as usual. The Enterprise look gives the Editor's font_family IBM Plex Mono this way. In a test, FakePluginHost.setKitDefault(String, String, Object) gives a look default and FakePluginHost.lookDefaultProblems(String) lists the ones the plugin could not use.

    Saving

    Setting.set(Object) writes a new value to the file, keeping its comments, and returns a CompletableFuture that completes on the UI thread once the setting's handle shows the value. It fails with IllegalArgumentException when the kind rejects the value, with the message SettingKind.check(Object) gives (for an integer, "Use a whole number from min–max."), and with IllegalStateException or IOException when the file changed on disk since it was read ("key changed on disk. Review the new value and try again."), has errors ("file has errors; fix them before saving settings."), would exceed 1 MiB, or the plugin has stopped. It is safe from any thread; the write itself happens off the UI thread.

    The plugin's page

    A running plugin that declared settings gets a generated page, Settings › Tools › name: one row per setting in declaration order, with its label, control, description and a way to reset it to its default, and a heading wherever the section changes. Apply saves the changed values to the file. A plugin the user meant to run but that is not running (waiting for a review, skipped, failed or held back by safe mode) gets a page that says "Start name to edit its settings.", gives the reason and offers Open in Editor for the file.

    A plugin that needs more than rows gives a page of its own with PluginSettings.page(SettingsPanel), once, while it starts. Settings calls SettingsPanel.create(SettingsPanelHost) the first time the page is shown in each opening of Settings; the page returns a view. SettingsPanelHost.row(Setting) gives the standard row for a declared setting, bound to the page's unsaved value, and Settings saves those on Apply itself. SettingsPanelHost.stage(Setting, Object) sets an unsaved value from a control of the plugin's own and SettingsPanelHost.changed() says the page's modified state changed. SettingsPanel.modified(), SettingsPanel.apply() and SettingsPanel.reset() cover only state of the plugin's own beyond its declared settings; SettingsPanel.dispose() runs when Settings closes the page.

    SettingsPanel.pendingChanged() runs after a standard row handles the user's edit, choice, list action, Browse… or Reset, once SettingsPanelHost.pending(Setting) returns the result and the row shows its validation (an invalid edit leaves the pending value as it was). Rebuild there whatever the page shows from pending values, as the Editor's page does. The plugin's own stage calls do not trigger it. It needs SDK 0.18.3.

    Services

    Plugins build on each other through services: a provider publishes an interface from a package it exports, and a plugin that requires the provider looks the service up. This is how Jasper's own features compose: Remote and File Server take credentials from the Credential Vault, Remote opens remote files in the Editor, Project Index lists projects on Remote's saved hosts, and Shell History saves commands as snippets. A third-party plugin can use those services, or publish its own, the same way. PluginContext.services() is the plugin's Services.

    Providing a service

    Put the interface, and the values it uses, in a package of their own and list it under exports. Only that exact package is visible to other plugins; a subpackage must be listed too, and everything else in the plugin stays private.

    id = "dev.example.notes"
exports = ["dev.example.notes.api"]
    package dev.example.notes.api;

import java.util.List;

/** What other plugins may ask of Notes. Call it on the UI thread. */
public interface NotesApi {
    /** @return the titles of the saved notes */
    List<String> titles();
}

    Publish during start, on the UI thread:

    List<String> titles = new ArrayList<>(List.of("Runbook", "On-call rota"));
context.services().publish(NotesApi.class, () -> List.copyOf(titles));

    Services.publish(Class, Object) gives every consumer the same instance; Services.publishPerConsumer(Class, Function) gives each consumer its own, made by a factory that Jasper calls on the UI thread just before that consumer starts, with the consumer's PluginInfo, so the provider knows who is asking (the Vault's grants are per plugin this way). A factory that returns null gives that consumer nothing. Jasper refuses a publication outside start, of a class that is not an interface, of an interface that is not in one of the provider's exported packages, and of an interface another plugin already published. Publications become visible only when start returns normally, so no consumer sees a service from a plugin that failed to start; they last until Jasper quits, with no withdrawal.

    Using a service

    A consumer lists the provider under requires and compiles against its exported package. Its class loader then sees that package, and only while the provider is loaded.

    requires = [{ id = "dev.example.notes", version = ">=1.0", optional = true }]
    /** Every line that names Notes's classes is in here, so a missing Notes plugin is caught in one place. */
final class NotesStatus {
    static String summary(Services services) {
        try {
            return services.find(NotesApi.class).map(api -> api.titles().size() + " notes").orElse("Notes is not running");
        } catch (NoClassDefFoundError absent) {
            return "Notes is not installed";
        }
    }
}

    Look services up in start: Jasper starts the providers a plugin requires first and prepares its instances before its start, and Services.find(Class) and Services.require(Class) are then cache reads, safe from any thread. find is empty when no provider the plugin requires offers the interface; require throws ServiceUnavailableException. A plugin sees services only from plugins it lists under requires.

    A hard requirement guarantees the provider: the consumer does not load without it. With optional = true the consumer loads either way, so it must survive the provider's absence. When the provider did not load, its classes do not exist for the consumer, and the first line that names them throws NoClassDefFoundError, even a lambda that only takes one as a parameter; keep every use of them behind one guard, as above. An optional requirement's version range is not checked, so a consumer that calls a method added in a later provider version catches NoSuchMethodError too, as Remote does for newer Editor methods.

    Topics between plugins

    A provider can also publish events: a plugin publishes on topics whose id starts with its own id and a dot, and any plugin may subscribe. Put the Topic constant and its payload type in the exported package; the Vault's VaultApi.LOCK_STATE_CHANGED (dev.jasper.vault.lock-state) is one.

    package dev.example.notes.api;

import dev.jasper.sdk.events.Topic;

/** The topics Notes publishes. */
public final class NotesEvents {
    /** @param count how many notes there are now */
    public record NotesChanged(int count) { }

    /** Published after every change to the notes. */
    public static final Topic<NotesChanged> CHANGED = Topic.of("dev.example.notes.changed", NotesChanged.class);

    private NotesEvents() { }
}
    // The provider, from any thread:
context.events().publish(NotesEvents.CHANGED, new NotesEvents.NotesChanged(3));

// A consumer, on the UI thread (behind the same guard when its requirement is optional):
context.events().subscribe(NotesEvents.CHANGED,
    changed -> context.log().log(System.Logger.Level.INFO, changed.count() + " notes"));

    Delivery is queued: handlers run later on the UI thread, in one order for the whole application, never during Events.publish(Topic, Object). There is no replay, so a late subscriber reads the current state from the service and then listens. One topic id carries one payload type; using it with another throws. Jasper's own topics are AppEvents (jasper.app.theme-changed and jasper.app.config-reloaded), Activities.TOPIC, Activities.CONNECTIONS and the TerminalEvents, which need terminal.observe.

    The bundled plugins' APIs

    Four bundled plugins export an API package. Their types are in the Bundled plugin APIs part of this reference; how each behaves for its users is in plugin APIs.

    PackageServiceWhat it offersRequires line
    dev.jasper.vault.apiVaultApi, one instance per consumerThe vault's lock state and its topic; unlocking; the credentials' descriptors, without secrets; a credential once the user allows the consumer to use it, once or always; a credential picker anchored on a control; importing SSH keys as managed keys{ id = "dev.jasper.vault", version = ">=0.2", optional = true }
    dev.jasper.editor.apiEditorOpening a local file, or a document the consumer reads and writes (EditorDocument), in an editor tab; reopening the consumer's documents from Recent Files; answering Open in Editor… first; offering a file source's places in the Editor's chooser; resolving the relative images and links of a Markdown preview through the consumer's document (EditorDocument.resolveRelative(String)){ id = "dev.jasper.editor", version = ">=0.7", optional = true }
    dev.jasper.remote.apiRemoteProjectsThe saved host and folder of an SSH pane; whether a host is connected; listing a remote work tree; looking for marker files; opening a remote file in the Editor or a terminal in a remote folder{ id = "dev.jasper.remote", version = ">=0.12", optional = true }
    dev.jasper.snippets.apiSnippetServiceLooking a snippet up by name; appending a snippet; the Snippets palette scope's id and row ids, for reopening the palette on a snippet{ id = "dev.jasper.snippets", version = ">=0.1", optional = true }

    The ranges shown are the highest a bundled consumer declares; Remote declares >=0.2 for the Editor. The SDK release carries no jar for these packages: their classes are in each provider's plugin jar, which the application holds in its bundled plugins/<id>/ folder (on macOS Jasper.app/Contents/app/plugins/<id>/). Compile against that jar as compileOnly, never bundle it, and test with a fake of the interface.

    Terminals

    PluginContext.terminals() is the plugin's view of Jasper's windows, tabs and panes. Finding them needs no capability; reading what a pane runs, typing into it, opening terminals and providing sessions do (see Capabilities). Every call is on the UI thread except the three that send input. For the user's side of panes and shell integration, see the terminal.

    Windows, tabs and panes

    Terminals.activeWindow() is the window the user used last, even while Jasper is in the background, and Terminals.activePane() the focused pane of its shown tab, when that pane is a terminal. Terminals.windows() lists the open windows in opening order, and Terminals.window(UUID), Terminals.tab(UUID) and Terminals.pane(UUID) find one by the id an event names. An action's ActionContext gives the window it ran in and the pane it concerns.

    WindowHandle, TabHandle and PaneHandle keep only an id; two handles for the same target are equal. A target can close at any moment: isOpen() tells, queries return the last known value, and commands to it are ignored. A window holds tabs, each holding panes, and each pane one item: a terminal or a plugin's content tab. WindowHandle.tabs() lists the items tab by tab in strip order, then pane by pane, as TabHandles; TabHandle.kind() says which kind an item is and TabHandle.terminal() is a terminal's one pane. WindowHandle.isMain() tells the main window, which keeps an empty workspace when its last tab closes, from a child window, which closes with its last tab. PaneHandle.focus() shows a pane's tab and focuses the pane, TabHandle.select() selects an item, and WindowHandle.toFront() raises a window. A window handle is also a WindowOwner, for dialogs and choosers over it. Jasper restores its windows at start and whenever the main window opens again: a restored terminal whose tab has not shown yet reports SessionState.NOT_STARTED until it first shows, and an item Jasper closed with its windows comes back under the same id, so drop a handle on TerminalEvents.TAB_CLOSED.

    Reading a pane

    With terminal.observe, PaneHandle.info() returns a PaneInfo snapshot:

    FieldMeaning
    titleThe title the program set, or the running command when it set none.
    workingDirectoryThe local folder the shell last reported, a hint that may no longer exist. A report counts as local only from a local shell whose report names no host, localhost or this machine.
    remoteDirectoryA RemoteDirectory (host and path) the shell reported, or the session's provider when the shell reports none; for display only. At most one of the two directories is present.
    columns, rowsThe grid size; 0 before the session starts.
    shellIntegrationWhether the shell reports its prompts and commands, which the command events need.
    kind, providerPluginIdSessionKind.LOCAL or SessionKind.PLUGIN, and the providing plugin.
    state, exitStatusSessionState.CONNECTING, RUNNING or EXITED, and the exit status once it exited with a known one.
    shellThe shell or program's label, such as zsh, or a provided session's title.

    PaneHandle.foregroundJob() asks the operating system for the program in the foreground and completes on a worker thread. TabHandle.title() is the tab's title as its header shows it. Both need terminal.observe; PaneHandle.selection(), the selected text, needs terminal.selection.

    Typing and pasting

    With terminal.inject, PaneHandle.sendText(String) types text as UTF-8 and adds nothing: end a command with "\r" to run it, or leave it at the prompt for the user. PaneHandle.sendBytes(byte[]) writes raw bytes, and PaneHandle.paste(String) pastes the way the user's paste does, bracketed when the program asked for that. The three are safe from any thread, and calls from one thread keep their order. Input to a pane whose session is not running (still connecting, or exited) is dropped.

    Opening tabs, splits and programs

    Terminals.openTab(WindowHandle, OpenRequest) opens and selects a tab; Terminals.split(PaneHandle, Direction, OpenRequest) splits a pane Direction.RIGHT or Direction.DOWN. Both return the new pane, or empty when the window or pane is gone (or, for a split, its session has ended) or the request names a profile Jasper does not list. A local request needs terminal.open:

    RequestStarts
    OpenRequest.local()The user's shell, where New Tab would start it. A split starts in the target pane's folder.
    OpenRequest.localIn(Path)The user's shell in an absolute folder.
    OpenRequest.localProfile(String)A detected shell profile, such as PowerShell 7 or a WSL distribution.
    OpenRequest.local(LocalSpec) with LocalSpec.running(List, Optional)A program instead of the shell, with the shell's environment. Each word is passed as it is, with no shell parsing it. Its pane closes when it exits with status 0 and stays open otherwise.
    OpenRequest.session(SessionSpec)A session the plugin provides; needs session.provide. See below.
     
    context.actions().register(ActionSpec.of("dev.example.tool.top", "Show Processes"), invoked ->
    context.terminals().openTab(invoked.window(),
        dev.jasper.sdk.terminal.OpenRequest.local(LocalSpec.running(List.of("top"), Optional.empty()))));

    A local request without a profile starts the user's default shell profile, for a split too, where the user's own Split repeats the target pane's profile. A profile id Jasper does not list opens nothing and is logged.

    Shell profiles

    Terminals.profiles() lists the shells Jasper detected for local panes, in the order its settings list them, as ShellProfileInfos with an id, a name, a ShellProfileInfo.Kind and a detail. On Windows they are powershell, pwsh (when PowerShell 7 is installed), cmd, cygwin (Cygwin Bash, when Jasper's own Cygwin is installed) and wsl:<name> for each WSL distribution; elsewhere login, the login shell; and last custom, the user's custom command. Detection can finish after the plugin starts: Terminals.onProfilesChanged(Runnable) runs after the first detection and after each later one whose result differs. Both need terminal.open. Remote lists the WSL distributions this way and opens them with localProfile.

    Shell environment

    String home = context.dataDirectory().toString();
context.terminals().environment(jasper -> Map.of("DEPLOY_TOOL_HOME", home));

    With terminal.environment, Terminals.environment(Function) adds variables to each new local shell and to each program a tab or split runs. The contributor runs on the UI thread for every launch, receives Jasper's own environment (read-only) and returns the variables to add, or null for none; it must not block or do I/O. A shell's environment is Jasper's own, then Jasper's variables, then the contributions, then the user's [terminal.env], then TERM and COLORTERM, so the user's settings win. A name must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*; TERM, COLORTERM, TERM_PROGRAM, TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION and names starting JASPER_ are reserved. Invalid names, reserved names and values holding NUL are dropped and logged once; when two plugins set one name, the first by plugin id wins. WSL profiles and provided sessions get no contributions. The Editor sets EDITOR this way.

    Terminal events

    Subscribing to any TerminalEvents topic needs terminal.observe. Events name windows, tabs and panes by id and arrive later on the UI thread; there is no replay, so read the current state from Terminals first.

    TopicPayloadWhen
    TerminalEvents.WINDOW_OPENED, TerminalEvents.WINDOW_CLOSED, TerminalEvents.WINDOW_ACTIVATEDTerminalEvents.WindowEventA Jasper window, the main window or a child window, opened, closed or became the active one.
    TerminalEvents.TAB_OPENED, TerminalEvents.TAB_CLOSED, TerminalEvents.TAB_SELECTEDTerminalEvents.TabEventAn item, terminal or content, opened, closed or became its window's active one.
    TerminalEvents.TAB_MOVEDTerminalEvents.TabMovedAn item moved to another window, instead of a close and an open; a moved terminal keeps its pane's id.
    TerminalEvents.PANE_OPENED, TerminalEvents.PANE_CLOSED, TerminalEvents.PANE_FOCUSED, TerminalEvents.BELLTerminalEvents.PaneEventA pane opened, closed, got focus or rang its bell.
    TerminalEvents.ACTIVE_PANE_CHANGEDTerminalEvents.ActivePaneChangedTerminals.activePane() changed; empty when there is none.
    TerminalEvents.TITLE_CHANGEDTerminalEvents.TitleChangedA pane's title changed.
    TerminalEvents.CWD_CHANGEDTerminalEvents.CwdChangedThe shell reported a new folder, local or remote.
    TerminalEvents.COMMAND_STARTED, TerminalEvents.COMMAND_FINISHEDTerminalEvents.CommandStarted, TerminalEvents.CommandFinishedA command started, and finished with its exit status, duration and folder. Shell integration only.
    TerminalEvents.SESSION_STATE_CHANGEDTerminalEvents.SessionStateChangedCONNECTING at each connect of a provided session, RUNNING when a session starts, EXITED when it ends.

    Shell History adds each command to its index from COMMAND_FINISHED as it finishes, beside what it reads from the shells' history files.

    Providing a session

    A plugin with session.provide can be a pane's session, as Remote is for SSH. Jasper owns everything a pane needs (the emulator, reading and writing, resizing, the status line while it connects, the Disconnected banner with Reconnect, closing); the plugin connects and hands over two streams. This example opens a TCP console port, such as a serial console server's:

    public final class ConsolePlugin implements Plugin {
    @Override public void start(PluginContext context) {
        context.actions().register(ActionSpec.of("dev.example.console.open", "Open Console Port"), invoked ->
            context.terminals().openTab(invoked.window(), dev.jasper.sdk.terminal.OpenRequest.session(
                new SessionSpec("console-1:7001", Optional.of("server"), ExitPolicy.KEEP_OPEN,
                    // Called on the UI thread for the first connect and every Reconnect: hand the work over at once.
                    pending -> context.background().execute(() -> connect(pending, "console-1", 7001))))));
    }

    private static void connect(PendingSession pending, String host, int port) {
        pending.status("Connecting to " + host + "…");
        Socket socket = new Socket();
        Subscription cancel = pending.onCancelled(() -> close(socket));
        try {
            socket.connect(new InetSocketAddress(host, port), 10_000);
            var exited = new CompletableFuture<Integer>();
            // From here on Jasper owns the connection and calls close exactly once.
            pending.attach(new TerminalConnection(socket.getInputStream(), socket.getOutputStream(),
                (columns, rows) -> { }, exited, () -> { close(socket); exited.complete(0); }));
        } catch (IOException failure) {
            pending.fail("Could not reach " + host + ":" + port + ": " + failure.getMessage());
        } finally {
            cancel.close();
        }
    }

    private static void close(Socket socket) {
        try { socket.close(); } catch (IOException ignored) { }
    }
}

    The pane appears at once, showing the status text (initially "Connecting…") and Cancel. The SessionSpec's connector is called on the UI thread while openTab runs, and again for every Reconnect or Retry, each time with a fresh PendingSession; it must not block. The spec's title is the pane's title until the program sets one, its icon (a semantic icon name) is the tab's, and its ExitPolicy decides what happens when the session ends: KEEP_OPEN shows how it ended and offers Reconnect, CLOSE closes the pane's tab. With SessionSpec.withRestore(RestoreState) the session's tab is saved with Jasper's windows, and the plugin's restorer opens it again; Jasper connects it when its tab is first shown.

    • One outcome per attempt. Exactly one of PendingSession.attach(TerminalConnection), PendingSession.fail(String) and cancellation takes effect; later calls are ignored. Every method is safe from any thread, also after the plugin stopped. fail shows the message with Retry (or Reconnect after an earlier session); a connector that throws fails the attempt with its message.
    • Cancellation. The user's Cancel, the pane closing, the plugin stopping or Jasper quitting cancels the attempt. PendingSession.onCancelled(Runnable) handlers run once, on Jasper's cleanup thread, to abort a blocking connect. Cancelling before any session was shown closes the pane, unless Jasper restored it with its tab.
    • Ownership. attach hands the connection over whatever happens: when the attempt was already cancelled or ended, Jasper closes it at once without reading it. Jasper calls close exactly once, on its cleanup thread; release everything the session holds there.
    • Threads. TerminalConnection's output is read on the session's reader thread and may block; close must unblock it. input and resize are used only on the session's writer thread, which flushes after every write. Input waits in a 4 MiB queue; a write that does not fit is dropped whole and the pane says "Input dropped: the remote side is not accepting input". Request TerminalConnection.TERM (xterm-256color) for a remote pseudo-terminal, and pass PendingSession.columns() and PendingSession.rows() as its first size.
    • Ending. When exited completes, Jasper keeps reading output for up to two seconds, then closes the connection; when the output ends first, it waits up to two seconds for exited, then closes it. The pane shows "Disconnected (exit N)", "Disconnected: The connection ended: message" when exited completed exceptionally, or "Disconnected: The connection ended without an exit status" when the output ended without one.
    • Folders. PendingSession.reportRemoteDirectory(RemoteDirectory) gives the pane a remote folder to show until the shell reports its own; it never becomes a local folder. A remote shell with Jasper's shell integration reports its folder and commands, and they arrive as remote folders and command events.

    Palette

    The command palette searches scopes. Jasper's own Commands scope lists every action, the bundled plugins add theirs (SSH hosts, tunnels, files, recent files, shell history, snippets, vault logins, file servers), and a plugin with palette.contribute adds its own through PluginContext.palette(). A scope answers each query with rows and offers up to three verbs on them; a verb can ask for a few values first in a small form, a step. The palette appears as the card in the default look and as the Run window in the Enterprise look; both show the same scopes. For the user's side, see the command palette.

    How users reach a scope

    The palette shows either no scope chip, searching everything, or one scope's chip. A query with no chip searches every scope that takes part in All (ScopeSpec.withInAll(boolean)), each as a section headed by its label, in order: Commands first, then contributed scopes in registration order; the list holds at most 200 rows, and a scope with more gets a "More in Label…" row that switches to its chip. The empty query shows "Recently used" and "Most used" rows (or "Suggested" ones when nothing was used yet). A scope's chip comes from:

    • typing its label and > at the start of the query (greetings > hello; the label is matched ignoring case, or as the only label starting with what was typed);
    • its shortcut action (ScopeSpec.withShortcutActionId(String)): while the palette is open, that action's shortcut switches to the scope's chip; while it is closed the action runs and usually opens the palette on the scope;
    • Palette.open(WindowHandle, String, Optional, Optional) from the plugin's code;
    • a "More in Label…" row, and the Run window's menu of scopes.

    A scope

    public final class GreetingsPlugin implements Plugin {
    private static final String SCOPE = "dev.example.greetings.scope";
    private static final String OPEN = "dev.example.greetings.open";
    private static final List<String> GREETINGS = List.of("good morning", "hello", "hi there");

    @Override public void start(PluginContext context) {
        // Register the action first: the scope names it, and its shortcut then reaches the scope both ways.
        context.actions().register(ActionSpec.of(OPEN, "Greetings…").withDefaultBinding("cmd+alt+y"),
            invoked -> context.palette().open(invoked.window(), SCOPE, Optional.empty(), Optional.empty()));
        context.palette().register(new PaletteScope() {
            @Override public ScopeSpec spec() {
                return ScopeSpec.of(SCOPE, "Greetings", "Search greetings",
                        List.of(new PaletteVerb("paste", "Paste"), new PaletteVerb("paste_run", "Paste and run")))
                    .withShortcutActionId(OPEN).withItemNoun("greeting");
            }
            // Runs on the UI thread for every keystroke: rank what is in memory, never read files here.
            @Override public PaletteResults search(String query, PaletteQuery palette) {
                String needle = query.strip().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT);
                var rows = new ArrayList<PaletteRow>();
                for (String greeting : GREETINGS)
                    if (greeting.contains(needle)) rows.add(PaletteRow.of("greeting." + greeting, greeting).withToken(greeting));
                return new PaletteResults(rows, needle.isEmpty() ? Optional.of("Greetings") : Optional.empty(), Optional.empty());
            }
            // Pasting needs a pane to paste into: the one the palette was opened from.
            @Override public boolean available(PaletteRow row, PaletteVerb verb, PaletteQuery palette) {
                return palette.target().isPresent();
            }
            @Override public void execute(PaletteRow row, PaletteVerb verb, PaletteQuery palette) {
                palette.target().ifPresent(pane -> {
                    pane.paste("echo '" + row.token() + "'");
                    if (verb.id().equals("paste_run")) pane.sendText("\r");
                });
            }
            @Override public Subscription onChanged(Runnable listener) { return () -> { }; }
        });
    }
}

    The plugin declares palette.contribute, and terminal.inject for the paste. Palette.register(PaletteScope) reads the ScopeSpec once and adds the scope to every window's palette; closing the registration removes it, and the plugin's scopes go when it stops. The id starts with the plugin's id and a dot, the shortcut action must be one the plugin registered before, the icon must be a known name, and an id already in use is refused.

    The spec

    PartMeaning
    id, labelThe scope's namespaced id, and the name its chip, section heading and prefix use.
    placeholderThe card's query hint while the scope's chip is shown.
    verbsOne to three PaletteVerbs with distinct ids, bound in order to Enter, Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Linux and Windows) and Shift+Enter. At most one has the PaletteVerb.Role.SPLIT role, the split-pane variant of the first verb, and never the first.
    monospaceRowsRows are data values, such as commands or paths, which the card draws in the data face.
    inAllWhether a query with no chip searches this scope; true for ScopeSpec.of(String, String, String, List).
    inRecentsWhether the empty query may offer the scope's rows, and whether running one is recorded (see below). A scope outside All is never in recents.
    shortcutActionIdOne of the plugin's actions whose shortcut reaches the scope.
    description, icon, hue, itemNounPresentation hints: the Run window shows the description as its help line, a square of the hue before each row (the manifest's icon_hue when the hue is NONE) and "Noun: …" in its detail line; it offers the SPLIT verb as "Open in a split pane". The card shows the label and none of these. The icon must be a known name, but neither view draws it.

    Searching

    PaletteScope.search(String, PaletteQuery) returns PaletteResults: at most 200 PaletteRows in display order, an optional section label (a heading over the rows while the scope's chip is shown) and the row to select first. The PaletteQuery says which window the palette is in, which pane it was opened from (target), how many rows the scope may return (maxResults: 200 on its own chip, its share of the 200 in All, 50 when Jasper looks a recent use up again) and whether to show macOS glyphs. Jasper cuts the answer to maxResults.

    A row has an id (unique in one answer, at most 256 characters), a title, an optional detail shown after it, a tag at the right (such as a shortcut), an icon, an enabled flag (a disabled row is dimmed and cannot run) and a token, any object of the scope's, which comes back unchanged with the row. The target pane is a handle bound to the scope's plugin: typing or pasting into it needs terminal.inject.

    Every PaletteScope method runs on the UI thread and must do no I/O: a scope that reads files keeps an index, refreshes it in the background, and tells the palette with the listener PaletteScope.onChanged(Runnable) gave it, which reruns an open query. PaletteScope.activated(PaletteQuery) is called when the palette opens on the scope's chip, or on All while the scope takes part, a good moment to ask the index for a refresh. Calls are contained: a failing search shows no rows for the scope.

    Running a verb

    When the user runs a verb, Jasper first asks PaletteScope.available(PaletteRow, PaletteVerb, PaletteQuery) again; false refreshes the list instead. It then asks PaletteScope.step(PaletteRow, PaletteVerb, PaletteQuery): a PaletteStep replaces the list with a small form, and the step's completion does the work; with none, the palette closes and PaletteScope.execute(PaletteRow, PaletteVerb, PaletteQuery) runs.

    @Override public Optional<PaletteStep> step(PaletteRow row, PaletteVerb verb, PaletteQuery palette) {
    if (!verb.id().equals("rename")) return Optional.empty();
    return Optional.of(new PaletteStep("Rename " + row.title(),
        List.of(new PaletteStep.Field("name", "New name", row.title())),
        (values, done) -> {
            String name = values.get("name").strip();
            if (name.isEmpty()) { done.accept(PaletteStep.Result.error("Enter a name")); return; }
            rename(row, name);
            done.accept(PaletteStep.Result.reopen(SCOPE, Optional.of("item." + name), Optional.empty()));
        }));
}

    The step's fields are plain text fields; Tab and Shift+Tab move between them. The completion receives the values by field name and must answer exactly once, from any thread: PaletteStep.Result.done() closes the palette, PaletteStep.Result.error(String) keeps the form open with the message, and PaletteStep.Result.reopen(String, Optional, Optional) closes it and opens it again on a scope, selecting a row. A completion that throws before it answers shows "The plugin could not complete this step."; an answer that arrives after the user left the step is dropped.

    Recents

    Running a row of a scope with inRecents records the scope id, row id and title, with a count and the time, in command-history.toml in Jasper home (at most 50 uses; ids and titles longer than 512 characters are not recorded). The empty query ranks those uses by frequency and recency, and finds each again by searching its scope for its title and matching the row id; a row the scope no longer returns drops out. So keep row ids stable, and turn recents off with ScopeSpec.withInRecents(boolean) for rows that should not be written to disk, as Shell History does for commands.

    Opening the palette

    Palette.open(WindowHandle, String, Optional, Optional) opens the palette in a window on a scope, any plugin's or jasper.commands, or with no scope chosen with jasper.all, with an optional query and row to select; it also needs palette.contribute. On the card, opening the scope that is already showing dismisses it instead; the Run window focuses its field. An unknown scope id is ignored, and so is a request for a window that is not the active one while its palette is closed.

    Testing

    The test kit, jasper-sdk-testkit-0.21.0.jar, runs a plugin headless in a unit test. Its FakePluginHost is a single-threaded stand-in for Jasper's plugin runtime with the same rules: queued event delivery, topic ownership, services committed only after a successful start, rollback and a closed context after a failed one, capability checks and namespaced ids. The test scripts the workstation (windows, panes, settings, commands) and reads back what the plugin contributed as plain lines. The kit depends only on the SDK; put both jars on the test classpath, as the quick start's build does. See also the test kit's README.

    A test

    The plugin under test types a configured command into a pane from the pane's context menu, and prints it from a jasper subcommand:

    package dev.example.deploy;

import dev.jasper.sdk.plugin.Plugin;
import dev.jasper.sdk.plugin.PluginContext;
import dev.jasper.sdk.settings.EditorHint;
import dev.jasper.sdk.settings.Setting;
import dev.jasper.sdk.settings.SettingKind;
import dev.jasper.sdk.settings.SettingSpec;
import dev.jasper.sdk.ui.ActionSpec;
import java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;

public final class DeployPlugin implements Plugin {
    static final String TYPE = "dev.example.deploy.type";

    @Override public void start(PluginContext context) {
        Setting<String> command = context.settings().declare(SettingSpec.of("command",
                SettingKind.text(text -> !text.isBlank(), "Enter a command."), "make check")
            .label("Check command").editor(EditorHint.technical()));
        context.actions().register(ActionSpec.of(TYPE, "Type Deploy Check"),
            invoked -> invoked.pane().ifPresent(pane -> pane.sendText(command.get())));
        context.menus().terminalContext().add(TYPE);
        context.commandLine().handle("deploy-check", call -> {
            call.out(command.get() + "\n");
            return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(0);
        });
    }
}
    package dev.example.deploy;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;

import dev.jasper.sdk.Capabilities;
import dev.jasper.sdk.PluginInfo;
import dev.jasper.sdk.terminal.PaneInfo;
import dev.jasper.sdk.terminal.SessionKind;
import dev.jasper.sdk.terminal.SessionState;
import dev.jasper.sdk.testing.FakePluginHost;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.OptionalInt;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.UUID;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class DeployPluginTest {
    private static final String ID = "dev.example.deploy";
    private static final PluginInfo INFO = new PluginInfo(ID, "Deploy", "1.0.0", Set.of(Capabilities.TERMINAL_INJECT));

    /** Declares the manifest's subcommand, as Jasper would, then starts the plugin. */
    private static void start(FakePluginHost host) {
        host.declareSubcommand(ID, "deploy-check", "Print the deploy check command");
        host.start(INFO, Set.of(), Set.of(), new DeployPlugin());
    }

    @Test void typesTheConfiguredCommandIntoThePane() {
        try (var host = new FakePluginHost()) {
            UUID window = host.addTerminalWindow(), tab = host.addTerminalTab(window, "build");
            UUID pane = host.addTerminalPane(tab, new PaneInfo("zsh", Optional.empty(), Optional.empty(), 80, 24, true,
                SessionKind.LOCAL, Optional.empty(), SessionState.RUNNING, OptionalInt.empty(), "zsh"));
            host.setSetting(ID, "command", "make deploy-check");
            start(host);

            assertThat(host.menu("context")).containsExactly("item:" + DeployPlugin.TYPE);
            assertThat(host.invoke(DeployPlugin.TYPE, window, pane)).isTrue();
            assertThat(host.sent(pane)).containsExactly("write:make deploy-check");
            assertThat(host.failures()).isEmpty();
        }
    }

    @Test void reportsABlankCommandAndUsesTheDefault() {
        try (var host = new FakePluginHost()) {
            host.setSetting(ID, "command", " ");
            start(host);

            assertThat(host.settingsReports(ID)).containsExactly("command: Enter a command.");
            var call = host.call("deploy-check", List.of(), Path.of("/work"));
            assertThat(call.exit()).isCompletedWithValue(0);
            assertThat(call.out()).isEqualTo("make check\n");
        }
    }
}

    Threads

    The thread that calls the host plays the UI thread. Nothing happens behind the test's back: published events wait until FakePluginHost.flush() delivers them (including those the deliveries publish), and background tasks wait until FakePluginHost.runBackground() runs them, one after another, on the calling thread. Run the plugin's start, and the test, on the Swing event dispatch thread instead when the plugin uses its UiKit: the kit's views (FakeKit, FakeKitView) require the real UI thread.

    @Test void buildsItsPanel() throws Exception {
    SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait(() -> {
        try (var host = new FakePluginHost()) {
            host.start(INFO, Set.of(), Set.of(), new TargetsPlugin());
            host.addTerminalWindow();
            host.openPanel("dev.example.tool.targets");
            assertThat(host.panelView("dev.example.tool.targets")).isPresent();
            assertThat(host.failures()).isEmpty();
        }
    });
}

    Starting and stopping

    FakePluginHost.start(PluginInfo, Set, Set, Plugin) starts a plugin as Jasper would, with its identity and capabilities, the ids of its hard and optional requirements, and the instance. A plugin whose hard requirement is not active is not started; a start that throws is rolled back. Start providers before their consumers: each consumer receives the services of the providers it names, made by their factories. FakePluginHost.stopAll() stops every plugin in reverse order, and FakePluginHost.close() also delivers what is queued and deletes the temporary folder that holds the plugins' data directories (FakePluginHost.FakePluginHost(Path) uses a folder the test owns instead). FakePluginHost.failures() lists every contained failure (throwing starts, stops, handlers, factories and background tasks) as a line; assert it is empty.

    Where the fake differs from Jasper

    • Background tasks run one at a time when the test asks; in Jasper each runs at once on a virtual thread of its own, so tasks can overlap.
    • The fake checks the calling thread only for the kit's views, which need the event dispatch thread, and for Appearance's colours, palettes, workspace opacity and theme subscriptions, which need the thread that made the host or the event dispatch thread (Appearance.variant(), Appearance.workspaceVariant(), Appearance.presentation() and Appearance.terminalTypography() answer any thread), and Appearance.onTerminalTypographyChanged(Consumer), which needs the event dispatch thread. Calls Jasper refuses off the UI thread with IllegalStateException (registrations, subscribing, publishing services, handling subcommands, terminal queries, the clipboard) succeed in the fake from any thread.
    • Services: the fake does not check that a service's interface is in one of the provider's exported packages, and an absent optional provider's classes are still on the test classpath, so the NoClassDefFoundError path cannot be tested with it.
    • Settings live in memory; the fake writes no file. A value of the wrong TOML type rejects only that setting, where Jasper rejects the whole file; FakePluginHost.settingsReports(String) words integer, number, choice and list rejections with the kind's own message, where Jasper uses its own wording (see Settings); set completes at once; and number values keep double precision. A look default the plugin cannot use is listed by FakePluginHost.lookDefaultProblems(String), where Jasper logs it as a warning.
    • Palette calls receive maxResults 5 and macOS glyphs, and FakePluginHost.executeInScope(String, String, String, UUID, UUID) skips the available check.
    • Platform.openInEditor(Path) runs on the calling thread; FileSource.connect(String, WindowOwner) always receives a window; provided panes report 80 × 24; cancellation handlers run at once.
    • An unavailable subcommand's message names the plugin's id rather than its name.
    • The fake has no active tool window: Panels.toggle(String, WindowHandle) and PanelHost.show() from a panel's own toggle action only toggle or show it, also under FakePresentations.CLASSIC, where Jasper activates a showing panel that is not the active tool window instead of hiding it.

    Distribution

    A plugin ships as a zip of its jars: the plugin's own jar, which holds plugin.toml, and every library it bundles. Users install it from Settings › Plugins; Jasper installs it at the next launch into plugins/<id>/jars/ in Jasper home.

    Building

    The quick start's build has two packaging tasks, both made of the plugin jar and its runtime classpath, the libraries in implementation:

    TaskWritesFor
    stagePluginbuild/plugin/<id>/jasper --plugin-dir build/plugin/<id> while developing
    pluginZipbuild/distributions/<id>-<version>.zipUsers: Install from Zip…

    The SDK is compileOnly: Jasper supplies it, and a plugin must not bundle it. Loading refuses a jar that defines classes in dev.jasper.sdk, dev.jasper.app, dev.jasper.terminal, dev.jasper.buddy, java, javax or jdk, or in a package one of the plugin's dependencies exports, and a class file larger than 16 MiB. A plugin's own packages may be anything else; the bundled plugins use dev.jasper.<name>.

    The zip

    • The jars lie at the zip's root or all in one folder, nothing deeper. Only .jar entries are unpacked; other files, names starting with . and anything under __MACOSX are ignored.
    • Jar names use only letters, digits, spaces and ., _, +, -; no name appears twice.
    • At most 4,096 entries, 256 jars and 512 MiB unpacked.
    • Exactly one jar holds a valid plugin.toml at its root, and its sdk range includes the installing Jasper's SDK.

    A zip that breaks a rule is refused with the reason, for example "The zip must hold the plugin's jars at its root or in one folder", "Not a Jasper plugin: …" or "Name version needs SDK range; this Jasper has SDK 0.21.0", and nothing is installed.

    Installing

    1. The user chooses File › Manage Plugins… (or Manage Plugins… in the command palette), then Install from Zip… in the Plugins page's Plugin options menu (its More button), and picks the zip.
    2. Jasper unpacks it into a staging folder and checks it as above.
    3. The Install name sheet shows the name, version, "From vendor", what the plugin asks to do (its capabilities in the user's words) and the warning that a plugin is not sandboxed. Install records the user's consent to exactly those capabilities and stages the plugin; the Plugins page shows "Install at restart".
    4. At the next launch, before any plugin loads, the jars move into plugins/<id>/jars/, and the plugin loads.

    A zip dropped into plugins/ in Jasper home is installed at the next launch with the same checks but without the sheet, so a new plugin waits as "Needs review" until the user reviews it; a zip that is not a usable plugin is renamed <name>.zip.rejected. The user's side of all this, including disabling and removing, is in plugins.

    Updating

    An update is a zip of the same id with a higher version, installed the same way; the sheet adds "This replaces the installed version when Jasper restarts." At the next launch its jars replace the old ones; the settings file plugins/<id>/<id>.toml and the data/ folder stay. The install sheet asks for every capability the new version declares. A dropped-in update that declares a capability the user has not allowed waits for a review before it loads; one that declares the same or fewer keeps the consent. Since each id loads once per launch, the higher version wins when the same plugin is also bundled or in --plugin-dir.

    The Java runtime

    Packaged Jasper runs plugins on its own trimmed JetBrains Runtime 25; the Java runtime lists exactly the modules a plugin may rely on. That is all of Java SE plus the charsets, locale data, ZIP file system, PKCS#11 and smart-card providers, Kerberos and JAAS login modules, DNS and RMI naming, socket options, the JDK HTTP server, sun.misc.Unsafe, and JFR, JMX and attach. The compiler and the other development tools (jdk.compiler, so ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler() returns null), the debugger (jdk.jdi, jdk.jdwp.agent), jdk.dynalink, jdk.incubator.vector and the JetBrains Runtime's JCEF are not there. A library that needs a missing module fails with NoClassDefFoundError in the packaged application, although it works under a development run on a full JDK; bundle a jar that provides it instead.

    On macOS and Windows the packaged JVM loads JNA's native library from Jasper's own copy (JNA 5.14.0). A plugin that bundles JNA bundles that version: another version fails to load its native part when it is the first in the process to initialise JNA. Start terminals through PluginContext.terminals() rather than a pseudo-terminal library of your own.

    Versions

    This reference documents SDK 0.21.0. The release jars carry the version in their names (jasper-sdk-0.21.0.jar) and as their manifests' Implementation-Version, and JasperSdk.VERSION holds it in code. That field is a compile-time constant, so a plugin that reads it gets the version it was compiled against, not the version of the Jasper it runs in. The SDK is at 0.x, which carries no compatibility promise. Javadoc @since tags in the API reference name the SDK version that added a type or member.

    The sdk range

    Every manifest says which SDK versions the plugin runs on, as a range. Build against SDK 0.21.0 and declare:

    sdk = ">=0.21.0, <0.22"

    That admits 0.21.0 and every later 0.21 version, and nothing from 0.22 on. A plugin that uses something only a later 0.21 version has starts its range there. Every bundled plugin declares sdk = ">=0.21.0, <0.22". 0.19.0, 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 are breaking boundaries: 0.19.0 makes a window's tabs terminal and content tabs alike (TabHandle.kind() and TabHandle.terminal() in place of a tab's pane list), 0.20.0 gives Jasper one main window and child windows in place of plugin windows (WindowHandle.isMain(), TabPlacement, ContentTab.moveToNewWindow()), and 0.21.0 makes tabs hold panes, adds split items (Windows.splitItem(SplitItemSpec, BiConsumer)) and saves the workspace (RestoreState, Windows.restorer(String, TabRestorer), SessionState.NOT_STARTED).

    FormMeaning
    >=0.18.0, >0.18.0, <=0.18.2, <0.19, =0.18.0A comparator and a version of one to three numbers; missing numbers are 0, so <0.19 means <0.19.0.
    >=0.18.0, <0.19Comparators separated by commas; every one must hold.
    ""An empty range admits every SDK version.

    A bare version such as "0.18.0" is not a range and makes the manifest invalid, and so does a version with a pre-release or build suffix. The version of a requires entry uses the same syntax.

    How Jasper checks

    Jasper compares the range with its own SDK version twice:

    • When a user installs the plugin. Install from Zip… refuses a zip whose range excludes this Jasper's SDK: "Name version needs SDK range; this Jasper has SDK 0.21.0". Nothing is installed.
    • At every launch. A plugin whose range excludes the SDK, wherever it was found, does not load. Its status line in the log and its row in Settings › Plugins say Skipped, and the Plugin problems group posts "Name was not started" with the reason, "needs SDK range; this is SDK 0.21.0", and Open Plugins. Plugins that require it, other than optionally, are skipped too.

    The range is the author's word. When it admits this SDK, loading still refuses a plugin whose classes refer to SDK types or members this SDK no longer has: Jasper posts "Name could not be loaded", naming the class, the missing type or member and the SDK version to rebuild it for. A call to a method this SDK lacks fails when it runs, as a LinkageError, which Jasper contains and reports like any other failure of the plugin.

    API reference

    Every public type and member, read from the Javadoc of SDK 0.21.0. Plugins compile against dev.jasper.sdk; tests use dev.jasper.sdk.testing from jasper-sdk-testkit; the bundled plugins' exported API packages are reached through Services.

    Plugin SDK jasper-sdk

    The API every plugin compiles against. It depends only on the JDK. Plugins implement Plugin and functional callbacks; Jasper implements everything else.

    package dev.jasper.sdk

    Leaf values shared by every SDK package: the SDK version, plugin identity, the capability names and the exception a gated call throws without one, the theme variant, the owner a dialog is parented to and the subscription returned by every registration. This package depends on no other SDK package.

    interface Subscription

    Long-running work a plugin volunteers to show: begin an activity, report progress, end it once; or announce a connection, report its state as it changes and close it.     Activities

    dev.jasper.sdk.activity
    interface Activities

    Begins activities, announces connections and lists the running activities. Anyone may subscribe to TOPIC and CONNECTIONS; only handles returned by begin and connection publish to them, so each lifecycle is well-formed and its source is verified.

    When an activity succeeds or fails, the host posts its outcome as a notification in the plugin's <plugin-id>.activities group: INFO or ERROR, titled after the activity, with the final detail as content and the activity's action as a click on its body. A cancelled activity posts nothing, and neither does one the host failed because the plugin stopped or failed to start. The user can mute that group without muting the plugin's own notifications.

    package dev.jasper.sdk.files

    interface FileBrowser

The host calls home, list, stat, read, mkdir, resolve and close on one of its worker threads, one call at a time, never on the UI thread; they may block. abort may be called from any thread. parent and name must be pure and may be called on any thread.     package dev.jasper.sdk.palette

    Command-palette scopes contributed by plugins. A scope is one kind of searchable thing: it answers a query with rows, runs one of its verbs on a row and may show a small form first. Every method runs on the UI thread and does no I/O; a scope returns at most PaletteQuery.maxResults() rows, and the list scrolls through them all. Depends on dev.jasper.sdk, dev.jasper.sdk.terminal and dev.jasper.sdk.ui (for Nodes.Hue).

    PaletteScopeinterfaceOne kind of searchable thing, implemented by a plugin and registered through Palette.
    PaletteSteprecordA small form the palette shows instead of its list.
    PaletteVerbrecordOne thing a scope can do with a row.
    ScopeSpecrecordWhat a scope is: identity, wording, verbs and how it is reached.

    Opens the palette in window on scopeId. query replaces the query text and rowId selects the first row with that id. When that scope is already showing, the command palette dismisses instead and applies neither, while the Run window stays open, focuses its field and applies both.     record ScopeSpec(String id, String label, String description, String placeholder, List<PaletteVerb> verbs, boolean monospaceRows, Optional<String> icon, Optional<String> shortcutActionId, boolean inAll, boolean inRecents, Nodes.Hue hue, String itemNoun)

    What a scope is: identity, wording, verbs and how it is reached. The palette shows either no scope chosen (All), which searches every scope that takes part, or one scope's chip; the user chooses a scope by typing its label and >, with the scope's shortcut action, from a "More in …" row, or from the Run window's scope menu.

    Stringdescriptionone line the Run window shows as its help while this scope is chosen; may be empty
    Stringplaceholderthe command palette's query hint while this scope is chosen
    List<PaletteVerb>verbsone to three verbs with distinct ids, bound to Enter, Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Linux and Windows) and Shift+Enter; at most one is a PaletteVerb.Role.SPLIT verb, and never the first
    booleanmonospaceRowswhether rows are data values (commands, paths), which the command palette draws in the data face
    Optional<String>icona semantic icon name for the scope, checked at registration; neither palette view draws it
    Optional<String>shortcutActionIdone of the plugin's own actions: while the palette is open, that action's shortcut chooses this scope instead of running the handler (the command palette dismisses when this scope is already chosen); the Run window shows its shortcut beside the scope in its menu
    booleaninAllwhether a query with no scope chosen searches this scope too (since 0.8.0)
    booleaninRecentswhether the palette may offer this scope's rows before anything is typed, among the recently and most used items; only a scope in All is offered there (since 0.9.2)
    Nodes.Huehuethe hue of this scope's row squares where a presentation draws them; NONE takes the plugin's manifest icon_hue, and NEUTRAL without one (since 0.18.0)

    Services

    dev.jasper.sdk.services
    interface Services

    The typed service registry. A publication lasts from the provider's successful start until it stops at shutdown; there is no withdrawal. Publications become visible only when the provider's start returns normally, so no consumer sees a service from a plugin that failed to start. Lookups are cache reads that run no provider code and are safe from any thread.

    Methods
    #<T> void publish(
        Class<T> api,
        T implementation)

    Publishes one shared implementation. UI thread, during the provider's own start only.

    Type parameters
    <T> service type
    Parameters
    api an interface from one of the provider's exported packages
    implementation the instance every consumer receives
    Throws
    IllegalStateException outside the provider's start
    IllegalArgumentException when api is not an interface the provider owns, or is already published
    #<T> void publishPerConsumer(
        Class<T> api,
        Function<PluginInfo, T> perConsumer)

    Publishes a per-consumer factory. The runtime calls it on the UI thread once for each plugin that declares requires on the provider, optional or not, just before that consumer starts, with the consumer's verified identity; a factory that returns null or throws gives that consumer no instance. This gives caller attribution; it is not a security boundary.

    Type parameters
    <T> service type
    Parameters

    package dev.jasper.sdk.settings

    PluginSettings

    dev.jasper.sdk.settings
    interface PluginSettings

    A plugin's settings, kept in plugins/<id>/<id>.toml under Jasper's home. A plugin declares every setting while it starts; the runtime then reads their values, reports values their kinds reject and keys nothing declares, and shows them in Settings. Jasper reads the file again whenever it changes. A file that is not valid TOML, or that gives a setting a value of the wrong TOML type, is reported and not applied: every setting keeps its last good value.

    SettingsPanel

    dev.jasper.sdk.settings
    interface SettingsPanel

    A plugin's own page in Settings, used instead of the page Settings generates from its declarations, in the manner of IntelliJ's Configurable. Every method runs on the UI thread. Settings saves the declared settings the page shows through SettingsPanelHost on Apply; modified, apply and reset cover only state of the plugin's own.

    Methods
    #UiView create(SettingsPanelHost host)

    Builds the page, once per opening of Settings, when the page is first shown.

    Parameters
    host standard rows and unsaved values for the plugin's declared settings
    Returns
    the page's component
    #default List<String> keywords()

    Extra words Settings' search matches for this page.

    Returns
    the words
    #default void highlight(String query)

    Marks what matches a search in the plugin's own controls; standard rows mark themselves.

    Parameters
    query the search text; blank clears the marks
    #default void pendingChanged()

    since 0.18.3

    Called after a standard row from SettingsPanelHost.row handles the user's input: a typed edit, a switch, a choice, a list action, a file from Browse… or Reset. SettingsPanelHost.pending already returns the resulting value and the row shows its validation; an invalid edit leaves the pending value as it was. Rebuild the descriptors that depend on pending values here. The plugin's own SettingsPanelHost.stage calls do not trigger it. Runs on the UI thread while the page is shown.

    #default boolean modified()

    Whether state of the plugin's own, beyond its declared settings, has unsaved changes.

    Returns
    true when Apply would save something of the plugin's own
    #default void apply()

    Saves state of the plugin's own; Settings saves the declared settings.

    #default void reset()

    Drops unsaved state of the plugin's own. Settings calls it just before dispose when it closes a page it showed without a successful Apply since the page last changed, as on Cancel; a page Settings never showed gets no reset. The panel outlives each opening of Settings, so this is where unapplied state of its own goes away.

    #default void dispose()

    Settings closed the page; release listeners. Unapplied state of the plugin's own was already dropped through reset.

    interface

    package dev.jasper.sdk.terminal

    Jasper's windows, tabs and panes as handles a plugin can query and drive, local tabs and splits it can open, sessions it can provide to a pane, the variables it can add to new local shells, and the jasper.terminal.* events. Finding a window, tab or pane needs no capability; reading, typing into and opening them do. Depends on dev.jasper.sdk and dev.jasper.sdk.events.

    PaneHandle

    dev.jasper.sdk.terminal
    interface PaneHandle

    One pane: the terminal of a terminal tab, so one session. Handles keep an id and no Swing object; two handles for the same pane are equal. A pane closes with its tab, at any moment: commands to a closed pane are ignored, queries return the last known value, and isOpen() tells. Input to a pane whose session is not running, before it starts, while it connects or after it ended, is dropped. A missing capability always throws. Once the plugin's context is closed, queries and commands throw IllegalStateException and the three sending methods do nothing. EDT only, except the three sending methods.

    #TabHandle tab()

    TerminalConnection

    dev.jasper.sdk.terminal
    record TerminalConnection(InputStream output, OutputStream input, BiConsumer<Integer, Integer> resize, CompletableFuture<Integer> exited, Runnable close)

    A connected session, handed to PendingSession.attach. From that call on Jasper owns it: it invokes close exactly once, whatever happens, so release everything that belongs to the session there. None of these members is ever called on the event thread: output is read on the session's reader thread, input and resize are used only on Jasper's writer thread for this session, and close runs on Jasper's cleanup thread. They must not touch Swing or event-thread-only SDK methods.

    Components
    InputStreamoutputremote to terminal, UTF-8; end of stream after the remote side ends. A read may block; close must unblock it
    OutputStreaminputterminal to remote; Jasper flushes after every write and never blocks the user on it
    BiConsumer<Integer, Integer>resizecolumns and rows of the pane, to pass to the remote pty; request TERM there
    CompletableFuture<Integer>exitedthe exit status; completing it exceptionally means the connection failed, and the message is shown
    Runnablecloseidempotent; unblocks a pending read; returns promptly
    Fields
    #static final String TERM = "xterm-256color"

    The terminal type to request on the remote pty.

    TerminalEvents

    dev.jasper.sdk.terminal
    final class TerminalEvents

    What happens in Jasper's windows, their tabs and terminal tabs' panes. Subscribing to any of these topics needs terminal.observe. Payloads name windows, tabs and panes by id, because a handle belongs to the plugin that obtained it; ask Terminals for one. Like every event they arrive later, on the event thread, and are not replayed: read the current state first, then listen.

    #Optional<PaneHandle> openTab(
        WindowHandle window,
        OpenRequest request)

    Opens a terminal in a new tab of the window, at the end of its tab strip, and shows it. A local request needs terminal.open and a session request session.provide; a local request naming a profile the host does not list opens nothing. A request with a command (LocalSpec.command()) runs that program instead of the shell, with the shell's environment, and its pane closes when the program exits with status 0.

    #Optional<PaneHandle> split(
        PaneHandle target,
        Direction direction,
        OpenRequest request)

    Opens a terminal in a new pane beside the target pane, in the target's tab, and selects it. A local request needs terminal.open and a session request session.provide; a local request naming a profile the host does not list opens nothing. A request with a command (LocalSpec.command()) runs that program instead of the shell, with the shell's environment, and its pane closes when the program exits with status 0.

    Parameters
    target the pane the new pane goes beside
    direction which side of the target pane the new pane takes
    request what to run
    Returns
