    #default List<ShellProfileInfo> profiles()

    since 0.9.1

    The shell profiles Jasper offers for local panes, platform default first: on Windows PowerShell (powershell), PowerShell 7 (pwsh), Command Prompt (cmd), Cygwin Bash (cygwin, from Jasper's own Cygwin) and each WSL distribution (wsl:<name>); on macOS and Linux the login shell (login); then Custom (custom), always last, which runs the program and arguments the user's settings name, or the platform's default shell when they name none. PowerShell 7, Cygwin Bash and the WSL distributions appear once a shell detection has found them. Needs terminal.open. UI thread only.

    Returns
    the profiles; empty when the host lists none
    #default Subscription onProfilesChanged(Runnable listener)

    since 0.9.1

    Calls the listener on the UI thread after a shell detection completes: the first one, which may finish after the plugin starts, and each later one (for example after the user asks Jasper to detect shells again) whose result differs, such as a WSL distribution or PowerShell 7 appearing or disappearing. Edits to the Custom shell settings may not be reported; read profiles() again when the current list matters. Needs terminal.open. The registration ends with the plugin.

    Parameters
    listener called with nothing; read profiles() again
    Returns
    the registration
    #default Subscription environment(Function<Map<String, String>, Map<String, String>> contributor)

    since 0.17.1

    Adds variables to each new local shell, and to each program a LocalSpec.command() runs. The contributor runs on the UI thread for every launch, must not block or do I/O, and receives Jasper's own environment, read-only; it returns the variables to add, and null adds nothing. A shell's environment is Jasper's own environment, Jasper's own variables, then the contributions, then the user's [terminal.env], then TERM and COLORTERM. A name must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*; TERM, COLORTERM, TERM_PROGRAM, TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION and names starting JASPER_ are reserved. An invalid or reserved name, and a value holding NUL, are dropped and logged once. When two plugins set one name, the first by plugin id wins and the other is logged. A contributor that throws adds nothing. WSL profiles and provided sessions get no contributions. Needs terminal.environment. UI thread only. The registration ends with the plugin.

    Parameters
    contributor given Jasper's own environment, returns the variables to add
    Returns
    the registration
    Throws
    MissingCapabilityException without terminal.environment

    interface Appearance

    Host-owned appearance values, the look Jasper runs with and the saved terminal typography. Declarative views follow these automatically; specialized content subscribes to refresh its domain palettes.

    Methods
    #Color color(SemanticColor role)

    Read a canonical semantic color on the UI thread.

    Parameters
    role canonical role
    Returns
    current color
    #Variant variant()

    The current variant; safe from any thread.

    Returns
    dark or light
    #EditorPalette editorPalette()

    since 0.8.5

    Host-owned colors for specialized document widgets. UI thread only.

    Returns
    the active workspace's editor palette
    #default Variant workspaceVariant()

    since 0.12.0

    Current workspace variant; safe from any thread.

    Returns
    workspace darkness
    #WorkspacePalette workspacePalette()

    since 0.12.0

    Workspace control colors. UI thread only.

    Returns
    the current workspace palette
    #SyntaxPalette syntaxPalette()

    since 0.12.0

    Workspace syntax colors. UI thread only.

    Returns
    the current syntax palette
    #default double workspaceOpacity(Component component)

    since 0.14.1

    How opaque the workspace behind component is: 1 unless the component is in the workspace area of a translucent window (where terminals and hosted content tabs live), in which case paint the component's own background with this alpha (the window shows the desktop through it). Chrome, tool windows and side panels stay opaque and report 1. Changes, including the component moving to another window, are reported through onWorkspaceChanged. UI thread only.

    Parameters
    component a component of this plugin's, shown or not
    Returns
    the opacity in effect, from 0.1 to 1
    #default Subscription onWorkspaceChanged(Consumer<Variant> handler)

    since 0.12.0

    Reports workspace changes, including changes within the same variant and of workspaceOpacity, on the UI thread.

    Parameters
    handler receives the workspace variant after the new palettes are available
    Returns
    the registration, removed when closed or the plugin stops
    #Subscription onChanged(Consumer<Variant> handler)

    Runs the handler on the UI thread after every chrome or workspace theme change, including color changes within the same variant. Workspace opacity changes use onWorkspaceChanged.

    Parameters
    handler receives the new variant
    Returns
    the registration
    #Presentation presentation()

    since 0.18.2

    The look Jasper runs with, chosen at start: the same value for every plugin until Jasper restarts. Safe from any thread.

    Returns
    the presentation
    #TerminalTypography terminalTypography()

    since 0.18.3

    The saved terminal typography: the font, size, fallback fonts, ligatures and line height of Settings › Terminal › Font & Colors (terminal.font in config.toml), the same for every window and plugin. A terminal pane's temporary zoom does not change it. Safe from any thread.

    Returns
    the current saved typography
    #Subscription onTerminalTypographyChanged(Consumer<TerminalTypography> handler)

    since 0.18.3

    Runs the handler on the UI thread each time the saved terminal typography changes; terminalTypography() already returns the new value when it runs. A saved value equal to the current one notifies nobody, and registering delivers no initial value, so read terminalTypography() first.

    Parameters
    handler receives the newly saved typography
    Returns
    the registration, removed when closed or when the plugin stops; safe to close from any thread
    Throws
    IllegalStateException off the UI thread, or once the plugin has stopped

    record Column(String id, String title, Nodes.TextRole role, boolean numeric, double weight, Optional<Boolean> sorted)

    ContentTab

    since 0.8.5dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    interface ContentTab
    extends WindowOwner, AutoCloseable

    App-owned document tab, also a dynamic dialog/picker owner. All methods except close use the UI thread. Moving retains content, selection/undo state and this handle. Closed handles do not reattach content. The handle carries the owning plugin's authority over the tab, its terminal.open for Terminal Right and Down (split) included, so a plugin hands other plugins window(), not the tab.

    Methods
    #void setPresentation(ContentPresentation value)

    Sets what the tab shows: its title, preceded by a dot while dirty and followed by the detail, its icon and, as its tooltip, the location; while the tab is active, the window's title and header context follow it. Ignored once the tab is closed.

    Parameters
    value literal title, location and state
    #void setCommands(List<ContentCommand> commands)

    Replaces the content's commands. They appear in the tab's context menu; while the tab is active, a command's shortcut runs it ahead of the Jasper actions bound to the same key, the command palette's shortcuts excepted (a disabled command's shortcut does nothing), and Jasper's Copy, Paste, Find, Find Next and Find Previous run the enabled command with the id copy, paste, find, find-next or find-previous. In a text field, the shortcut of a copy or paste command keeps the field's own clipboard behaviour. Ignored once the tab is closed.

    Parameters
    commands immutable snapshot of active-content commands
    #void setStatus(List<ContentStatus> items)

    Replaces the items the window's status bar shows while this tab is active. Ignored once the tab is closed.

    Parameters
    items immutable snapshot of status items
    #void setFocusTarget(Runnable focus)

    Sets what Jasper runs to focus the content, as when its tab is selected or its window is brought to the front; by default Jasper focuses the content's view.

    Parameters
    focus UI-thread callback focusing the editable content
    #void setRestore(Optional<RestoreState> state)

    since 0.21.0

    How the tab comes back when Jasper restores its windows, in place of what its ContentSpec.restore() said: a document saved under a new name names its new file. Empty: the tab is not saved.

    Parameters
    state the restore state, or empty
    #void select()

    Selects and raises the current host, focusing its content.

    #void moveToNewWindow()

    since 0.20.0

    A new child window takes the tab and its content. A child window's only tab, a tab with a modal prompt open and a tab being closed stay where they are.

    #void moveToMainWindow()

    since 0.20.0

    Move to Main Window: a new tab of the main window, at the end of its tab strip, takes the tab and its content, the main window restored first when none is open. A tab the main window holds, a tab with a modal prompt open and a tab being closed stay where they are.

    #void moveToNewTab()

    since 0.21.0

    Move Pane to New Tab (tabs and panes spec 9): the pane showing this item leaves its tab for a new tab right after it, which shows; nothing closes or leaves the window. Its tab's only pane, a tab with a modal prompt open and a tab being closed stay where they are (mayMoveToNewTab()).

    #boolean mayMoveToNewTab()

    since 0.21.0

    Whether moveToNewTab() would move this item, for a menu entry that shows disabled otherwise.

    Returns
    false for its tab's only pane, a tab with a modal prompt open, a tab being closed and a closed one
    #void split(
        SplitChoice choice,
        Direction direction)

    since 0.21.0

    Split with a choice beside this item (tabs and panes spec 8): selects it, then opens choice in a new pane on direction's side of its pane, as the Split lists' entries do: a terminal for SplitChoice.TERMINAL, else the split item's view, through its action. A closed tab, or one being closed, opens nothing. Whoever calls it, it runs with the owning plugin's authority over the tab, its terminal.open for Terminal Right and Down included, so hand other plugins window(), not the tab.

    Parameters
    choice one of Windows.splitChoices()
    direction the new pane's side
    Throws
    IllegalArgumentException when choice is not, or no longer, one of Windows.splitChoices()
    MissingCapabilityException when choice is SplitChoice.TERMINAL and the plugin lacks terminal.open: checked first, as Terminals checks it, so a closed tab's split is refused too
    #WindowHandle window()

    since 0.20.0

    The window that holds the tab; WindowHandle.isMain() tells the main window from a child window.

    Returns
    the window, or the last window that held the tab once it is closed; a window that is not open, with the id new UUID(0, 0), for a tab waiting for the main window to open or one no window could take back
    #boolean isActive()

    Whether the tab is active: the item of the focused pane in its window's shown tab.

    Returns
    whether the content is selected in its host
    #boolean isClosed()

    Whether the content has closed: by the user, through requestClose() or close(), with its window, or when the plugin stopped.

    Returns

    #CompletableFuture<Boolean> requestClose()

    Asks to close the content as Close Tab does: it closes unless this plugin's closing guard refuses, another close decision is pending, or a file chooser or modal dialog it owns is open.

    Returns

    Returns

    ControlState

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record ControlState(boolean visible, boolean enabled, boolean busy, String error)

    Presentation state; error carries validation prose, never secret content. A hidden, disabled or busy node also disables every node inside it. Enter in a Nodes.Form does not submit while a visible, enabled node in it is busy or has an error.

    Components
    booleanvisiblefalse hides the node and everything in it
    booleanenabledfalse disables the node and everything in it, so it reports no events
    booleanbusytrue while the node's work runs: it is disabled as if enabled were false
    Stringerrorvalidation prose, empty for none: a field, secret or choice shows it below itself and a toggle as its tooltip; each of them, and a button, also gives it as its accessible description. A PREVIEWS choice, and a SLIDER field where the look draws a slider (as the default look does), neither show it nor describe it
    Fields

    Visible, enabled, not busy and without an error.

    record CustomContent(String id, Nodes.CustomKind kind, JComponent component, AutoCloseable lifetime)

    Explicit specialized widget registration; appearance subscriptions refresh domain palettes.     Constants
    CENTERED
    A native dialog centred over its owner, sized to its content, which the user cannot resize, except that a modeless dialog whose content is a Nodes.FormKind.WINDOW form opens at a window's size, can be resized and remembers its bounds.
    ATTACHED_SHEET

    Nodes

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    final class Nodes

    The node types a ViewSpec is built from. A node says what a view shows and which UiEvents it reports, never how it is drawn: the host draws every node in the current look and theme, and the plugin answers events with UiView.update(ViewSpec). Nodes are immutable records with no pixel dimensions, delegates or secret values. Each record checks its own components when it is constructed, and ViewSpec checks the whole tree: node ids unique across the view, item references, and where a node may stand.

    Nested types
    • Nodes.Node sealed interface One node of a ViewSpec tree: a control, a text or a container of other nodes.
    • Nodes.TextRole enum A text's type role, which sets its font and colour.
    • Nodes.Hue enum A category colour from the theme's hues: it tints an icon's glyph, a chip, a swatch and the category tile some compositions set an icon on.
    • Nodes.IconSize enum An icon's size role.
    • Nodes.ButtonKind enum A button's treatment.
    • Nodes.StatusKind enum The state a StatusDot or a tree row's status shows: SUCCESS, WARNING and DANGER in the theme's status colours, IDLE in its idle status colour.
    • Nodes.FieldKind enum What a Field holds.
    • Nodes.ChoiceKind enum How a Choice is drawn.
    • Nodes.CardKind enum How a Card lays out its children.
    • Nodes.SelectionMode enum NONE keeps rows readable and scrollable but removes row selection, activation and the canvas focus stop.
    • Nodes.ListKind enum RESULTS is a one-line result list driven by an external field (a command palette): it never takes focus, the host moves its selection, a left press activates a row, and fixed row and heading heights keep it steady.
    • Nodes.FormKind enum PROMPT is a short, focused question (unlock, create) and PROMPT_COMPACT its compact form.
    • Nodes.LayoutRole enum VERTICAL stacks children top to bottom, and DETAIL a detail column's sections.
    • Nodes.SplitKind enum THREE_COLUMN places a manager window's rail, list and detail columns side by side; SIDEBAR_DETAIL is the same manager without its rail (its last child is the detail column, the others list columns).
    • Nodes.CustomKind enum What a Custom node hosts; the CustomContent registered for it has the same kind.
    • Nodes.ScrollPolicy enum A hint: STANDARD reserves the scroll bar's width; OVERLAY shows a transient thumb over the rows only while scrolling.
    • Nodes.Text record A run of passive text in a type role.
    • Nodes.Severity enum A message severity: INFO in the accent colour, WARNING and DANGER in the status colours.
    • Nodes.Icon record A glyph, or at the SWATCH size a square of its hue.
    • Nodes.ButtonPresentation enum How a button sits in its composition.
    • Nodes.Button record A push button: pressing it reports action as a UiEvent.Action.
    • Nodes.MenuButton record A button with a menu of MenuItems.
    • Nodes.StatusDot record A small round dot in its kind's status colour, such as whether a saved host is connected.
    • Nodes.Numeric record Bounds and shape of a NUMBER field: the kit admits only numbers of this shape and steps by step with the arrow keys, clamped to the bounds.
    • Nodes.FieldPresentation enum How a field sits in its composition.
    • Nodes.Field record A text entry: every edit reports UiEvent.Edited with the field's whole text.
    • Nodes.SecretKind enum INPUT is a masked single-line entry with a reveal control; CONFIRMATION is the same editable input without its own reveal control, following its reveal group.
    • Nodes.Secret record A secret entry or stored secret whose characters never appear in the descriptor: read them with UiView.withSecret, replace them with UiView.replaceSecret (which also sets a DETAIL secret's stored value) and erase them with UiView.clearSecret.
    • Nodes.ChoiceSearch record Type-to-filter configuration of a SEARCHABLE choice.
    • Nodes.PickerDensity enum A hint for a PickerFace's size: DEFAULT is a form's face, COMPACT a shorter face with smaller type and tile for a picker inline in a row.
    • Nodes.PickerFace record The closed face of a PICKER or DROPDOWN Choice, as display data only.
    • Nodes.PickerItemKind enum What a PickerItem row is.
    • Nodes.PickerItem record One selectable row of a PickerMenu; its id is also the Action emitted on explicit acceptance.
    • Nodes.PickerMenu record A searchable menu of rich rows, such as a PluginPopover's content for a PICKER choice: a search field over items, then a footer row after a hairline.
    • Nodes.Choice record One value from a set of options, drawn as its kind says.
    • Nodes.Toggle record A boolean, drawn as a switch or a checkbox as the look decides.
    • Nodes.Chip record A passive tag, such as a protocol or a badge: its label in the hue's colour on a tint of that hue (the Enterprise look boxes it and draws the label in capitals).
    • Nodes.Progress record A passive progress bar in the accent colour, with label as a caption under its trailing end.
    • Nodes.Strength record A passive four-segment meter, such as a password's strength, with label as a caption under its trailing end.
    • Nodes.Stack record Children laid out as role says.
    • Nodes.FormRow record A labelled form row: the label (with its caption under it) in the form's label column, the control beside it and an optional trailing cell after the control, which takes at most half the room beside the label; a row too narrow for that stacks them.
    • Nodes.SettingRow record A setting: its title and description, with the control at the row's trailing edge; the description wraps beside the control.
    • Nodes.Card record A grouped surface whose children stack top to bottom; the default look draws it as a rounded card.
    • Nodes.Section record A titled part of a view: the default look draws the title as a muted section label above the body, and the Enterprise look draws a section and its Card body as one box whose top edge the title breaks.
    • Nodes.Empty record Nothing to show yet, or a disconnected state: centred in its area, the icon on a tile, the title, the description and a row of actions.
    • Nodes.ItemList record Virtual row collection.
    • Nodes.Header record A Panel's one-line header: the title, the count, then context and primary, then a "More actions" menu button listing overflow when it has items.
    • Nodes.Panel record A panel, such as a tool window's content: the header at the top, the footer at the bottom, and between them the search or navigation row over the body.
    • Nodes.FormSubmission enum What Enter does at form level when the focused control does not take the key itself (see Form).
    • Nodes.Form record The content of a dialog, sheet or window: an optional hero, the sections, and a footer with a preview or a footnote at its leading edge and the action buttons at its trailing edge.
    • Nodes.Split record Two or more children arranged by kind: side by side as full-height columns, or for DOCUMENT stacked top to bottom, the first visible Custom, Empty or Split child, if any, filling the height the others leave.
    • Nodes.Table record Rows of cells under column headers, with an explicit selection mode and scroll policy.
    • Nodes.Tree record A tree of items; the user selects one item at a time.
    • Nodes.Breadcrumbs record A path of crumbs that can turn into a typed path.
    • Nodes.Separator record A thin rule between two items of an INLINE or ACTIONS stack, dividing a toolbar row into groups; never a stack's first or last child and never beside another separator.
    • Nodes.Notice record A message for the person reading a form or a pane: a severity, one sentence and at most one SECONDARY or LINK action.
    • Nodes.PropertyRow record One labelled value of Properties.
    • Nodes.Properties record A read-only list of labelled values, such as a selected host's properties.
    • Nodes.Custom record A slot for one specialised component that the plugin registers with UiView.registerContent(CustomContent): the content's id and kind must match this node's contentId and kind, and the component must have no parent and must not be registered in another slot.
    sealed interface

    Nodes.Node

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    sealed interface Node
    permits Nodes.Text, Nodes.Icon, Nodes.Button, Nodes.MenuButton, Nodes.StatusDot, Nodes.Field, Nodes.Secret, Nodes.Choice, Nodes.PickerMenu, Nodes.Toggle, Nodes.Chip, Nodes.Progress, Nodes.Strength, Nodes.Stack, Nodes.FormRow, Nodes.SettingRow, Nodes.Card, Nodes.Section, Nodes.Empty, Nodes.ItemList, Nodes.Header, Nodes.Panel, Nodes.Form, Nodes.Split, Nodes.Table, Nodes.Tree, Nodes.Breadcrumbs, Nodes.Custom, Nodes.Separator, Nodes.Notice, Nodes.Properties

    One node of a ViewSpec tree: a control, a text or a container of other nodes.

    Methods
    #String id()

    The node's id, never blank and unique across the whole view. The events a node reports name it by this id, except a UiEvent.Action, which carries the action key the node configures. An update keeps the mounted control, with its focus and caret, of a node whose id and node type stay the same, and also its kind for a Button, Field, Secret or Choice, whether its presentation is STEPPER, SLIDER or another for a Field, its kind and content id for a Custom, and its scroll policy for a Table. Any other node is mounted afresh.

    Returns
    the node id
    #ControlState state()

    The node's visibility, enablement, busy state and validation error.

    Returns
    the node's state
    enum

    Nodes.TextRole

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum TextRole

    A text's type role, which sets its font and colour. PROMPT_TITLE, DETAIL_TITLE, WINDOW_TITLE and PANEL_TITLE head a prompt, a detail column, a window and a panel; BODY is ordinary text and BODY_STRONG its emphasis; CHIP is the small type of a chip's label. LABEL and DESCRIPTION take the secondary text colour, CAPTION, COUNT, SECTION_LABEL, SUPPORTING and MONO_CAPTION the tertiary, and the other roles the primary. The MONO roles mark data values (hosts, ports, paths, commands), drawn in the data face.

NONE is no category: an Icon's glyph takes the secondary text colour, and a list row's leading RAIL or PROMPT icon, and a picker row's or face's icon, stands without the tile it otherwise sits on.

    Nodes.IconSize

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum IconSize

    An icon's size role. CAPTION stands beside caption text, CONTROL beside a control's or a row's text, RAIL in a rail or a list row, and EMPTY in an Empty state; a list row's leading RAIL or PROMPT icon sits on a tile in its hue unless the hue is NONE. PROMPT is the large icon: a prompt's header, a detail heading or a sheet's title. SWATCH (since 0.18.0) is a solid square of the icon's hue at caption size, such as a protocol's colour beside its name; its hue is not NONE and it takes no severity, and its name stays a valid icon name.

    Nodes.ButtonKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum ButtonKind

    A button's treatment. PRIMARY is the surface's main action: a Form's actions hold at most one, which the form's Enter presses (see FormSubmission). SECONDARY is a standard button, GHOST a quiet one, DESTRUCTIVE_GHOST a quiet one for a removal, and LINK a link. In the default look PRIMARY is filled in the accent colour and SECONDARY in the secondary button colour; GHOST, DESTRUCTIVE_GHOST and LINK have no resting fill, a DESTRUCTIVE_GHOST's text turns the danger colour, on a danger tint, on hover, and LINK is text in the link colour.

    Nodes.FieldKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum FieldKind

    What a Field holds. TEXT is one line of text. SEARCH is a search or filter field: its label is only its accessible name, and the default look draws a search glyph before the text. PORT admits digits only and is as wide as a port number, in the data face. PATH is a file path in the data face; a nonblank trailingAction adds a Browse… button that reports it, and Enter in the field passes on. TEXTAREA wraps over several lines, and Enter in it starts a new line. NUMBER requires a Numeric shape.

    SEARCH

    TEXTAREA

    Nodes.ChoiceKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum ChoiceKind

    How a Choice is drawn. DROPDOWN is a closed control whose popup lists the options. PICKER is a face whose click, Enter or Down reports its action, and the owner shows the options. SEARCHABLE is a dropdown whose open list narrows as the user types (see ChoiceSearch). PREVIEWS shows its options as tiles, an option with a preview as the miniature window it describes. EXCLUSIVE is a choice among two to four options, all of them visible. TABS (since 0.18.0) switches among two or more views of one thing (Overview and Details): it reports Selected, and the owner composes the chosen content.

    PICKER
    EXCLUSIVE
    SEARCHABLE
    PREVIEWS

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui

    How a Card lays out its children. FORM pads the card and stands its children (form rows, text) a row gap apart. SETTINGS holds SettingRows edge to edge, without gaps; the default look adds no padding and draws a hairline between them. MIXED holds both: its setting rows edge to edge, its other children padded.

    Nodes.FormKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum FormKind

    PROMPT is a short, focused question (unlock, create) and PROMPT_COMPACT its compact form. SHEET is a sheet's or a short dialog's content; without a hero it shows its title as its heading unless the dialog's own title bar carries it. FULL is a dialog's content, such as groups of fields, each a Section holding a Card. WINDOW has exactly one full-bleed content section, no hero, and a shared pinned footer. SETTINGS takes the generic form spacing; a plugin's own Settings page is a Stack with LayoutRole.SETTINGS_PAGE.

    Nodes.LayoutRole

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum LayoutRole

    VERTICAL stacks children top to bottom, and DETAIL a detail column's sections. INLINE, ACTIONS, FOOTER, NAVIGATION and JOINED_ACTIONS lay them side by side: ACTIONS is a row of buttons that wraps onto further rows when too wide; FOOTER is a status footer whose last child shortens to the width the others leave, its children stacking when it is too narrow; JOINED_ACTIONS draws its buttons as one joined group. PROMPT_HEADER is a prompt's header of icon, heading and message. SETTINGS_PAGE is a Settings page whose children are Sections holding SETTINGS Cards, and the other SETTINGS_ roles compose its parts. SUPPORTING keeps leading adornments natural-sized beside a wrapping final text/body child. ROUTE is a read-only route preview (a tunnel's path): a bordered strip on the input surface whose children are its steps, left to right, with the kit's arrow before every step after the first. A step is a stack whose leading Icon the kit shows on a category tile in its hue, its other children (Text) being the step's lines. The steps take equal columns, each later column opening with the arrow, and a step's lines truncate within its column.

    Constants

    INLINE
    ACTIONS
    PROMPT_HEADER
    DETAIL
    FOOTER
    NAVIGATION
    SUPPORTING
    JOINED_ACTIONS
    SETTINGS_PAGE
    SETTINGS_CONTROLS
    SETTINGS_TRAILING
    SETTINGS_GROUP_HEADER
    SETTINGS_FOOTER
    SETTINGS_NAVIGATION
    ROUTE

    Nodes.SplitKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum SplitKind

    THREE_COLUMN places a manager window's rail, list and detail columns side by side; SIDEBAR_DETAIL is the same manager without its rail (its last child is the detail column, the others list columns). DOCUMENT stacks them top to bottom for a document surface (an editor tab): every visible child takes its preferred height except the first visible Custom, Empty or Split child, which fills the height left over; hidden children take no space. The other children are the document's bars: an INLINE stack among them (directly, or as a row of a VERTICAL group) is one compact bar row whose first field or text fills the width the controls after it leave (the rows of one group line their fills up), with the panel search field's look for its fields and the panel action size for its buttons; a group stacks its rows without gaps and shows a passive (SelectionMode.NONE) list's rows as text lines; a hairline separates neighbouring children. An INLINE stack directly in a DOCUMENT split whose first child is an empty CAPTION text, followed by one or more Buttons and nothing else, is an action bar: the empty text pushes the buttons to the trailing edge, and while the split is narrower than the buttons the row scrolls sideways, bringing a button into view when it takes the focus.

    Constants
    SIDEBAR_DETAIL
    THREE_COLUMN
    DOCUMENT
    enum

    Nodes.CustomKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum CustomKind

    What a Custom node hosts; the CustomContent registered for it has the same kind. EDITOR admits a text component (a JTextArea, JTextPane or JEditorPane) or a canvas; TERMINAL, CHART and PREVIEW admit only a canvas: a custom-painted JComponent that is not a JPanel, a text component, a button, a label, a list, a table, a tree, a combo box, a spinner or a slider. A component in a JScrollPane is judged by the scroll pane's view. The host refuses anything else: ordinary controls are described with nodes.

    Constants
    EDITOR
    TERMINAL
    CHART
    PREVIEW

    Nodes.Text

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Text(String id, ControlState state, String text, Nodes.TextRole role, Optional<Nodes.Severity> severity, OptionalInt caret)
    implements Nodes.Node

    A run of passive text in a type role. Its whole text is its tooltip (in a list row, the row's tooltip takes its place). A MONO, MONO_SMALL or MONO_CAPTION text that does not fit is shortened at its start so its end stays in view (a form's preview at its end); other text that does not fit is shortened at its end. A present severity draws the text in that severity's colour (INFO the accent, WARNING and DANGER the status colours), as Icon.severity() tints a glyph, instead of its role's colour. A present caret (MONO and MONO_SMALL and MONO_CAPTION text only, from 0 to the text's length) draws a thin insertion bar in the text's colour after that many characters, as a command line shows its cursor.

    Nodes.ButtonPresentation

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum ButtonPresentation

    How a button sits in its composition. STANDARD is the kit's padded, minimum-height button. EMBEDDED is content-sized for a host arrangement that supplies the spacing (for example a row of inline links): no padding, focus-ring inset, minimum height or resting fill, and an icon-only embedded button draws its glyph at the row-glyph size. Keyboard focus still shows, as a hairline in the focus colour inside the button's bounds. CONTEXTUAL_EMBEDDED reserves the same mounted, focusable and accessible control, but paints it only while its containing item row is selected, hovered or keyboard-active, or while the button itself is hovered/focused. Outside an item row it behaves like EMBEDDED. It never changes action dispatch or selection. HELP is a button that opens help; the default look draws it round.

    Constants
    STANDARD
    EMBEDDED
    CONTEXTUAL_EMBEDDED
    HELP

    Nodes.Button

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Button(String id, ControlState state, String label, String icon, Nodes.ButtonKind kind, String action, String tooltip, Nodes.ButtonPresentation presentation, Optional<Nodes.Severity> iconSeverity, Optional<Boolean> selected)
    implements Nodes.Node

    A push button: pressing it reports action as a UiEvent.Action. A present iconSeverity tints the button's glyph with that severity's colour (as Icon.severity() does) at rest and on hover, instead of the kind's text colour; for example a favourite's warning star. The label keeps the kind's colour. A present selected makes it a toggle button (a search option such as match case): the kit paints the pressed treatment while it is true and reports its pressed state to assistive technology; a click reports the Action and the owner confirms the new state in its next update. Only GHOST and SECONDARY buttons take it.

    Nodes.FieldPresentation

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum FieldPresentation

    How a field sits in its composition. STANDARD shows the kit label (a SEARCH field never does) over a filled input. EMBEDDED leaves the visible label to the host's own arrangement (the label stays the accessible name). TRANSPARENT is EMBEDDED on a host surface that is the field's backdrop: no input fill, the outline and focus ring kept. TECHNICAL marks a data value (a host, port, path or command): standard geometry in the data face. PLAIN_PATH keeps PATH semantics and Browse with no leading folder; other kinds reject it. STEPPER and SLIDER (NUMBER only) are hints for how the number is offered.

    EMBEDDED
    TRANSPARENT
    TECHNICAL
    PLAIN_PATH
    STEPPER

    implements Nodes.Node

    A text entry: every edit reports UiEvent.Edited with the field's whole text. A NUMBER field states its Numeric shape; other kinds have none. alternateAction is what Shift+Enter in a single-line field runs (a find field's Previous); cancelAction is what Escape in the field runs. Blank passes either key on, to an enclosing stack or form. A nonblank listId names an ItemList in the same view: Up, Down, Page Up and Page Down in the field move that list's selection (reporting its Selected) while the focus stays in the field, and Enter keeps its meaning in the field. A TEXTAREA takes neither alternateAction nor listId, and a NUMBER field (whose arrows step it) takes no listId. A readOnly field (since 0.18.0) is focusable, selectable and copyable but never edited, so it reports no UiEvent.Edited; a STEPPER or SLIDER is never read-only.

    Components
    Stringidthe node id
    ControlStatestatethe node's state; a nonblank error shows under the field
    Nodes.FieldKindkindwhat the field holds
    Stringvaluethe field's text; the field shows a new value when an update changes it
    Stringhintthe placeholder shown while the field is empty, and its accessible description while it has no error; a STEPPER shows it instead as a unit after the value, and a SLIDER right after its value. Blank for none
    Stringlabelthe field's label and accessible name; the presentation decides whether it shows. Not blank
    StringtrailingActionwhat Enter in a single-line field runs, the field keeping the key; a PATH field's Browse… button reports it instead. Blank passes Enter on, to an enclosing form
    Optional<Nodes.Numeric>numerica NUMBER field's shape: present for NUMBER, empty for the other kinds
    Nodes.FieldPresentationpresentationhow the field sits in its composition
    StringalternateActionwhat Shift+Enter runs; blank for none
    StringcancelActionwhat Escape runs; blank for none
    StringlistIdthe id of the ItemList the field's Up, Down, Page Up and Page Down keys move; blank for none
    booleanreadOnlywhether the field shows its value without ever being edited

    Nodes.SecretKind

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum SecretKind

    INPUT is a masked single-line entry with a reveal control; CONFIRMATION is the same editable input without its own reveal control, following its reveal group. DETAIL is a read-only stored value, masked as a fixed row of dots that does not disclose its length, with a reveal control and an optional copy button. MULTILINE is an editable, wrapping secure-note area over the same wipeable storage, shown in clear, with no reveal or copy control, so it takes neither a reveal group nor a copy action. DISCREET_INPUT reserves reveal geometry and shows the control when nonempty or focused within.

    Constants
    INPUT
    DISCREET_INPUT
    CONFIRMATION
    DETAIL
    MULTILINE

    record PickerMenu(String id, ControlState state, String query, String placeholder, List<Nodes.PickerItem> items, String checkedId, String activeId, String noMatches, String footerLabel, String footerAction, String cancelAction)
    implements Nodes.Node

    A searchable menu of rich rows, such as a PluginPopover's content for a PICKER choice: a search field over items, then a footer row after a hairline. The kit does not filter: typing reports UiEvent.Edited naming this node, and the owner answers with the matching items. Up and Down move the active row, wrapping round and including the footer, and report UiEvent.Selected naming this node and the row; Enter or a left press accepts a row as UiEvent.Action with the row's id (footerAction for the footer); Escape reports cancelAction. While an input method holds uncommitted text these keys do nothing. The checked row (the current value) and the active row (the keyboard highlight) are distinct. At most nine rows show before the list scrolls.

    Stringquerythe search field's text; the field takes it whenever it changes

    A boolean, drawn as a switch or a checkbox as the look decides. A validation error in state replaces the tooltip. pending means a change is in flight while the domain confirms it (for example a tunnel starting): the control stays operable and reports the opposite of checked, which is always the confirmed state, and the default look shows the switch's knob midway on the warning colour.

    Nodes.ItemList

    since 0.18.0 for emptyTextdev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record ItemList(String id, ControlState state, Nodes.ListKind kind, List<ListItem> items, Set<String> selectedIds, String activateAction, List<MenuItem> contextActions, Nodes.SelectionMode selectionMode, Optional<Nodes.Button> addAction, OptionalInt visibleRows, String enterAction, String deleteAction, String detailsAction, String copyAction, String cancelAction, String emptyText)
    implements Nodes.Node

    Virtual row collection. MULTIPLE selects rows with Shift (a range) and Cmd (Ctrl on Linux and Windows) or Space (one row), without checkboxes; addAction is a footer, never a data item. A present visibleRows is how many selectable rows the viewport shows before it scrolls (headings above them add their own height); absent keeps the kit default. Headings are never selected and ORDERED lists have none. A present enterAction is what Enter on the focused row reports (after selecting it), so a double click and Enter can differ; blank keeps Enter as activateAction. A present deleteAction is what Delete and Backspace on the focused row report (an unselected row is selected first); blank passes those keys on. A plain left single click on a row also reports UiEvent.Clicked after its selection, except in a RESULTS list, which takes none of the row key actions either. An ORDERED list's move up, move down and remove commands report UiEvent.Reordered and UiEvent.Removed; the owner confirms them by updating the list. detailsAction, copyAction and cancelAction bind D, platform Copy and Escape only while the row canvas has focus; blank actions pass the key to an enclosing control. With no items the body shows emptyText as one muted line, above addAction; blank shows nothing.

    Nodes.FormSubmission

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum FormSubmission

    What Enter does at form level when the focused control does not take the key itself (see Form). PRIMARY presses the form's PRIMARY action, even while another of its buttons has the focus; NONE presses nothing. Either way, Enter on a focused Button goes to the form instead of pressing it, and Space presses it.

    Nodes.Form

    since 0.18.0 for footnotedev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Form(String id, ControlState state, Nodes.FormKind kind, String title, Optional<Nodes.Node> hero, List<Nodes.Node> sections, Optional<Nodes.Node> preview, List<Nodes.Button> actions, String cancelAction, Nodes.FormSubmission submission, String footnote)
    implements Nodes.Node

    The content of a dialog, sheet or window: an optional hero, the sections, and a footer with a preview or a footnote at its leading edge and the action buttons at its trailing edge. The window around it is the host's. The focus starts in the form's first visible, enabled Field, Secret or Choice that is not busy; call UiView.focus(String) to start elsewhere. With FormSubmission.PRIMARY, Enter presses the PRIMARY action unless the focused control takes Enter itself (such as a Field whose Enter runs its trailingAction, a Secret with a submitAction, a PICKER Choice, editing Breadcrumbs, or a list, table or tree row with an activate or Enter action; a Table with an activateAction keeps Enter even with no row focused), a popup is open, the focus is in a multi-line text area, or the form or a visible, enabled control in it is busy or shows an error, which also disables the PRIMARY button. Escape closes an open popup, or else reports cancelAction while the form is enabled and not busy; a focused control's own cancel action, or an enclosing Stack's, is reported instead.

    Components
    Stringidthe node id, unique in its view
    ControlStatestatevisibility and interaction state
    Nodes.FormKindkindthe form's layout, from a short prompt to a full window
    Stringtitlethe form's title, not blank. A SHEET without a hero draws it as its heading unless the host's title bar shows the dialog's title; other kinds do not draw it. A title bar shows the DialogSpec title.
    Optional<Nodes.Node>heroan optional block above the sections, such as a prompt's PROMPT_HEADER stack of icon, heading and message; a SHEET or FULL form's hero Text that only repeats the title is hidden while the dialog's title bar carries the title. A WINDOW form has none.
    List<Nodes.Node>sectionsthe body, top to bottom; a WINDOW form has exactly one, which fills the window. A Notice may stand here.
    Optional<Nodes.Node>previewan optional node at the footer's leading edge. A monospaced Text, such as an equivalent command (shortened at its end), and any preview of a WINDOW form stay beside the actions until the room there is narrower than the standard form label column, then move to their own line above them; any other preview moves there when it does not fit beside the actions. A form has a preview or a footnote, not both.
    List<Nodes.Button>actionsthe footer's buttons; at most one is PRIMARY
    StringcancelActionwhat Escape reports; blank for none
    Nodes.FormSubmissionsubmissionwhat Enter does at form level
    Stringfootnoteone plain line drawn muted at the footer's leading edge, such as an auto-lock note; blank for none

    since 0.18.0 for empty and emptyTextdev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Table(String id, ControlState state, List<Column> columns, List<TableRow> rows, Set<String> selectedIds, String activateAction, List<MenuItem> contextActions, Nodes.SelectionMode selectionMode, Nodes.ScrollPolicy scroll, Optional<Nodes.Empty> empty, String emptyText)
    implements Nodes.Node

    Rows of cells under column headers, with an explicit selection mode and scroll policy. Selecting rows reports UiEvent.Selected; with MULTIPLE selection Shift-click selects a range, and Cmd-click (Ctrl-click on Linux and Windows) or Space adds or removes one row. A plain left single click also reports UiEvent.Clicked, and a left click on a column header reports UiEvent.Sorted. A heading row (TableRow.heading()) groups the rows below it and is never selected, activated or offered a menu. With no rows the body shows empty or the muted line emptyText below the column headers, which stay.

    Nodes.Tree

    since 0.18.0 for columnsdev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Tree(String id, ControlState state, List<TreeItem> roots, Set<String> expandedIds, Set<String> selectedIds, String activateAction, List<Column> columns)
    implements Nodes.Node

    A tree of items; the user selects one item at a time. Selecting an item reports UiEvent.Selected, and a plain left single click also reports UiEvent.Clicked. A branch's disclosure control, and Right or Left on the focused branch, report UiEvent.Expanded; the owner answers with an updated expandedIds. A right click offers the item's own TreeItem.contextActions(); a tree has no shared menu. A non-empty columns shows a header over the rows: the first column titles the items, and each later column titles one of the items' TreeItem.trailing() values, in order, so an item has at most one value per column after the first. Clicking a column header reports UiEvent.Sorted, as a Table's does; the owner orders the items. Empty columns shows no header.

    Components
    Stringidthe node id, unique in its view
    ControlStatestatevisibility and interaction state
    List<TreeItem>rootsthe top-level items, in order; item ids are unique across the whole tree, nested at most 128 levels below the roots
    Set<String>expandedIdsthe expanded branches' ids, each a branch of this tree; a collapsed branch's children are not shown
    Set<String>selectedIdsthe selected items' ids, each an item of this tree
    StringactivateActionwhat a double click or Enter on an item reports after selecting it; blank for none
    List<Column>columnsthe header's columns, with unique ids; empty for no header

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Breadcrumbs(String id, ControlState state, List<Crumb> crumbs, String label, boolean editing, String value, String editAction, String submitAction, String cancelAction)
    implements Nodes.Node

    A path of crumbs that can turn into a typed path. Clicking a crumb reports UiEvent.Selected with its id; a crumb's context action reports only its UiEvent.Action (it does not navigate). Clicking the free area reports editAction. While editing the kit shows a text field holding value; when editing starts the kit focuses the field and selects its text, and UiView.focus(String) returns the focus to it. The field reports typing as UiEvent.Edited, Enter as submitAction and Escape or leaving the field as cancelAction. When the crumbs do not fit, the leading ones slide out so the last stays visible.

    Components
    Stringidthe node id, unique in its view
    ControlStatestatevisibility and interaction state
    List<Crumb>crumbsthe path, root first, with unique ids; the last crumb is the current location
    Stringlabelthe accessible name of the crumbs and of the field; not blank
    booleaneditingwhether the path shows as a text field instead of crumbs
    Stringvaluethe field's text; an update with a different value replaces what the field holds
    StringeditActionwhat a left click on the free area beside the crumbs reports, typically to start editing; blank for none
    StringsubmitActionwhat Enter in the field reports while editing; not blank while editing
    StringcancelActionwhat Escape in the field, or the focus moving to another control, reports while editing; not blank while editing

    Nodes.Custom

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Custom(String id, ControlState state, String contentId, Nodes.CustomKind kind, String accessibleName)
    implements Nodes.Node

    A slot for one specialised component that the plugin registers with UiView.registerContent(CustomContent): the content's id and kind must match this node's contentId and kind, and the component must have no parent and must not be registered in another slot. A scroll pane is judged by its view. An EDITOR slot admits a text area, text pane, editor pane or purpose-built canvas; the other kinds admit only a canvas: a component that is not a panel, text component, button, label, list, table, tree, combo box, spinner or slider. The host sets the component's foreground to the theme's text colour and its background to the theme's input colour at the workspace opacity, and makes it opaque only at full opacity, on every theme or opacity change and every move. The content's lifetime closes when the node leaves the view, when an update changes its contentId or kind, or when the view closes.

    Components
    Stringidthe node id, unique in its view
    ControlStatestatevisibility and interaction state
    StringcontentIdthe id the registered content carries; not blank and unique among the view's Custom nodes
    Nodes.CustomKindkindthe kind of component the slot admits
    StringaccessibleNamethe slot's accessible name; not blank
    record

    #void toggle(
        String panelId,
        WindowHandle window)

    since 0.7.2

    Toggles this plugin's registered panel in the main window, creating it lazily; a child window's request shows it and brings the main window to the front. Requests from a closed window have no effect. Called from the panel's own toggle action (PanelSpec.withToggleActionId), as its handler runs, under a look with flush tool windows a toggle that shows the panel also makes it the active tool window, as a stripe click does, and a toggle of a showing panel that is not the active tool window activates it instead of hiding it (since 0.18.2).

    Parameters

    window the window the request comes from, the main window or a child window

    IllegalStateException when the context is closed or the caller is off the UI thread

    #boolean copy(String text)

    since 0.16.1

    Puts text on the system clipboard. UI thread only; elsewhere it throws IllegalStateException. When the clipboard cannot be written, for example while another program holds it, a failure is posted in the plugin's notification group, never thrown.

    Parameters
    text the text, possibly empty
    Returns
    whether the text is on the clipboard
    Throws
    NullPointerException when text is null
    #boolean copySecret(String text)

    since 0.16.1

    As copy, for text that should not linger, such as a password or a decrypted value. Jasper clears the clipboard 30 seconds later (retrying briefly while another program holds it), and tries once when the plugin stops and once when Jasper quits, in each case only if the clipboard still holds this text. A later copy, by the user or by any plugin, is left alone.

    Parameters
    text the text, possibly empty
    Returns
    whether the text is on the clipboard
    Throws
    NullPointerException when text is null
    #Optional<String> clipboardText()

    since 0.16.1

    The clipboard's text. Needs clipboard.read. UI thread only; elsewhere it throws IllegalStateException.

    Returns
    the text, or empty when the clipboard holds no text or cannot be read
    Throws
    MissingCapabilityException without clipboard.read
    #default Subscription editor(FileEditor editor)

    since 0.17.1

    Makes this plugin the editor Jasper opens files with: config.toml, the plugin settings files, the custom VM options file, every openInEditor and a Cmd-click (Ctrl-click on Linux and Windows) on a file path in a local terminal pane go to editor first, on the UI thread; a click brings the path's line and the clicked window. A clicked path comes from program output, and an OSC 8 link's target can differ from the text shown, so an editor edits the file and never runs it. One at a time: a bundled plugin's registration replaces a plugin's that is not bundled; otherwise the first stays and any later one, this plugin's own included, throws. When the editor returns false or throws, when no plugin provides one, and when Jasper waited 30 seconds for the UI thread's answer, the desktop opens the file as before; for a click it edits the file or shows it in the file manager instead, and never opens it. Needs editor.provide. UI thread only. The registration ends with the plugin.

    Parameters
    editor opens a file
    Returns
    the registration
    Throws
    IllegalStateException when another plugin already provides the editor (The editor is already provided by <plugin id>), and off the UI thread
    MissingCapabilityException without editor.provide

    Presentation

    since 0.18.2dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record Presentation(boolean classic, Presentation.Icons icons, Presentation.ToolWindows toolWindows, Presentation.TitleBar titleBar, Presentation.Menus menus, Presentation.ToolbarSearch toolbarSearch, Optional<String> uiFace, Optional<String> dataFace, int bodySize, int toolbarHeight)

    Facts about the look Jasper runs with, read through Appearance.presentation(). The look is chosen at start and stays for the run. The faces, the body size and the toolbar height are the look's own: the user's settings for them are not reported. The title bar and the menus are the look's in the Normal view with the platform's default decorations; the user's decoration and view-mode settings are not reported.

    Components
    booleanclassicwhether the look starts from the classic catalog: classic controls and IntelliJ Classic's layout
    Presentation.Iconsiconsthe icon set the look paints with
    Presentation.ToolWindowstoolWindowshow tool windows are reached
    Presentation.TitleBartitleBarthe title bar on this platform
    Presentation.Menusmenuswhere the menus are on this platform
    Presentation.ToolbarSearchtoolbarSearchhow the toolbar offers Search Everywhere: the field, or IntelliJ Classic's icon button
    Optional<String>uiFacethe look's UI face for its regular weight, a name java.awt.Font accepts, or empty for the platform face; the user's font setting is not reported
    Optional<String>dataFacethe look's data face for its regular weight, a name java.awt.Font accepts, or empty for the platform face (Font.MONOSPACED); the user's font setting is not reported
    intbodySizethe look's body text size in points, from 6 to 96; the user's font size is not reported
    inttoolbarHeightthe look's default toolbar height in pixels, from 28 to 64; the user's toolbar height is not reported

    ShortcutContext

    since 0.11.0dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record ShortcutContext(ShortcutContext.Kind kind, Optional<String> id)

    Where an action's shortcut applies. A key can belong to several actions in different contexts. Where focus is, the most specific applicable one runs: a panel or content context, then terminal(), then global(). A key whose action does not apply where focus is reaches the focused component instead, for example the shell in a terminal pane. So does a key whose action is disabled, except in a terminal pane: there the key does nothing, so the shell never receives it as a control character.

    TabPlacement

    since 0.20.0dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    enum TabPlacement

    Where Windows.openTab(ContentSpec, WindowOwner, UiView, TabPlacement) puts a new content tab (tabs and panes spec 11). A content tab is an item, the one a pane shows: a window holds tabs, and each tab holds panes. A tab already open for the same key is selected where it is, whatever the placement.

    Constants
    NEW_TAB
    In a new tab of the owner's window, or of the main window when there is no owner: at the end of its tab strip and shown, the main window's empty workspace taking it in its place.
    SPLIT_RIGHT
    In a new pane to the right of the focused pane of that window's shown tab.
    SPLIT_DOWN
    In a new pane below the focused pane of that window's shown tab.
    NEW_WINDOW
    In a new child window of its own, opened for it; the owner's window is not touched. The topics report WINDOW_OPENED, then TAB_OPENED in the new window.
    functional interface

    TabRestorer

    since 0.21.0dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    @FunctionalInterface
interface TabRestorer

    Rebuilds a plugin's saved tabs when Jasper restores its windows (workspace tabs spec 13 and 14): at start, and whenever the main window opens again after it closed. Registered with Windows.restorer for one restorer kind; called on the UI thread for a saved tab of that kind:

    • once for each saved tab while its window is restored, before that window shows;
    • again when the user presses Retry on its placeholder, while the window shows;
    • when the plugin itself opens a tab while no Jasper window is open, which restores the windows first: inside that call, before the call's tab opens.
    Methods
    #Optional<String> restore(RestoreRequest request)

    Opens one saved tab again, before returning, the way the plugin opened it: a content tab with Windows.openTab(ContentSpec, WindowOwner, UiView), or a provided session with Terminals.openTab, with the same restore state. The first content tab the plugin opens meanwhile is the saved tab, whatever window or placement it names, and so is the first session it opens in request.window(); Jasper puts it where it was saved, with the selection it had, and a session's tab connects when it is first shown. Open only that tab: while the restorer runs, the window being restored takes no other, so another content tab opens where an owner-less one would, and another session does not open. Ask the user nothing here (no dialog, sign-in or prompt); a tab that needs one opens waiting, as a session that offers Reconnect does. It runs on the UI thread, so it must not block (a quick check that a local file exists is fine, but reading it or calling the network is not); a tab that needs either opens waiting. The saved tab stays in the window being restored while the restorer runs, so a move asked of it then does nothing. When the tab cannot come back now for a reason the plugin expects (its file or host is gone), return why instead of opening it: a placeholder in its place says so, with Retry, and nothing is reported as the plugin's failure. Opening nothing without a reason, or throwing before the tab opens, also leaves a placeholder; a throw is the plugin's failure. A restorer that has opened its tab keeps it whatever it then returns or throws, except an Error other than a LinkageError: that closes the tab, which comes back as a placeholder, and is the plugin's failure as a throw is, while the other saved tabs and windows come back. A VirtualMachineError (such as OutOfMemoryError or StackOverflowError) is not contained: the tab it opened is closed and the error propagates, so the restore of that window fails. Jasper then keeps the saved windows aside and, for the main window, opens a new one in its place.

    Parameters
    request the window, the saved title and the restore state
    Returns
    empty once the tab is open again; else why it cannot come back, which its placeholder shows after "could not restore this tab:"
    record

    TableRow

    since 0.18.0 for cellNodes and headingdev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record TableRow(String id, Map<String, String> cells, Optional<String> icon, boolean muted, Optional<List<MenuItem>> contextActions, String tooltip, Map<String, Nodes.Node> cellNodes, Optional<TableRow.Heading> heading)

    Immutable table row descriptor: one row of a Nodes.Table.

    A column's content is a plain cell (cells) or a cell node (cellNodes), never both. A cell node is a Nodes.Text, Nodes.StatusDot, Nodes.Icon or Nodes.Chip, an INLINE Nodes.Stack of those, or a DROPDOWN Nodes.Choice without a rich face, which reports UiEvent.Selected and is drawn without a border (its value, then its chevron) until it is hovered or focused. Cell nodes are view nodes, so their ids are unique in the view; cellNodes iterates in column-id order.

    A heading row (heading(String, String, OptionalInt, String)) has a Heading and nothing else: it spans the row, groups the rows below it, and is never selected or activated.

    Components
    Stringidthe row's id, unique in its table; reported in UiEvent.Selected and UiEvent.Clicked, and named by the table's selectedIds
    Map<String, String>cellseach column's plain text by column id, drawn in the column's text role; a column with neither a cell nor a cell node is empty
    Optional<String>iconthe name of an icon drawn before the first column's text when that column is a plain cell; absent for none
    booleanmutedtrue draws the plain cells and Text cell nodes in the de-emphasized text colour while the row is not selected, for example entries that cannot be chosen
    Optional<List<MenuItem>>contextActionspresent is the row's own menu with unique ids, offered on it whether or not it is selected, and empty means the row has none; absent, the table's menu, which acts on the selection, is offered while the row is selected
    Stringtooltipthe row's literal tooltip and accessible description, shown over every cell; blank for none
    Map<String, Nodes.Node>cellNodeseach column's cell node by column id
    Optional<TableRow.Heading>headingpresent makes this a heading row

    ToolbarItem.View

    since 0.18.0dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record View(ToolbarViewFactory factory)
    implements ToolbarItem

    A small group of the plugin's own controls, one per window with a toolbar (the main window), such as a session choice with a Connect button. The factory runs when such a window opens, and for each one already open from inside add, never for a window nobody sees, and the view closes with its window or with this registration. Its root is an INLINE Nodes.Stack of LABEL Nodes.Texts, DROPDOWN, SEARCHABLE or PICKER Nodes.Choices, at most one PRIMARY Nodes.Button and any number of icon-only GHOST Buttons (a blank label with an icon and a tooltip, since 0.18.1), Nodes.MenuButtons and Nodes.Separators. When it mounts the view the host refuses any other tree without an exception to the plugin: it records the refusal, naming the node, closes the view and that window shows none. UiView.update throws IllegalArgumentException naming the node and keeps the tree. A view never moves into the overflow menu: it hides while the toolbar is too narrow for it.

    Components
    ToolbarViewFactoryfactorybuilds one window's view
    Constructors

    Rejects a null factory.

    functional interface

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    sealed interface UiEvent
    permits UiEvent.Action, UiEvent.Edited, UiEvent.Selected, UiEvent.Toggled, UiEvent.Expanded, UiEvent.Removed, UiEvent.Reordered, UiEvent.SecretChanged, UiEvent.Clicked, UiEvent.Sorted

    Typed user intent. Action ids are configured action keys. All payload-bearing events identify the owning node; consumers resolve its configured action through the current ViewSpec.     • UiEvent.Selected record A new selection: the option of a Nodes.Choice, the keyboard-active row of a Nodes.PickerMenu, the clicked crumb of Nodes.Breadcrumbs, or the selected rows of a Nodes.Table, Nodes.Tree or Nodes.ItemList.
    • UiEvent.Toggled record A Nodes.Toggle the user switched; Space on a list row whose trailing slot holds exactly one switch switches it too.
    • UiEvent.Expanded record Expansion intent from a branch's disclosure or the Right and Left arrow keys: id is the tree owner, itemId is local to that tree.
    • UiEvent.Removed record Ordered-list removal intent from an ORDERED Nodes.ItemList's Remove command: a row's own or, in a look that gives the list a side column of commands, the column's Remove acting on the selected row (a list whose selection mode is NONE keeps the commands on its rows).
    • UiEvent.Reordered record Ordered-list move intent from an ORDERED Nodes.ItemList's Move up or Move down command: a row's own or, in a look that gives the list a side column of commands, the column's Move Up or Move Down acting on the selected row.
    • UiEvent.SecretChanged record The content of a Nodes.Secret changed.
    • UiEvent.Clicked record A plain left single click on a table, tree or item-list row (not a RESULTS list, a list or table whose selection mode is NONE, or a heading), reported after its Selected: id is the owner, itemId the row.
    • UiEvent.Sorted record Sort intent from a left click on a column header: id is the table or tree owner, columnId the clicked column.

    ViewSpec

    dev.jasper.sdk.ui
    record ViewSpec(Nodes.Node root)

    A validated immutable view tree. Node ids are global; item ids are local to their owning control. The constructor throws IllegalArgumentException unless:

    • node ids are unique in the view, and so are Nodes.Custom content ids;
    • the view nests at most 128 levels below its root and holds at most 100,000 nodes;
    • a Nodes.Notice stands only in a Nodes.Form's sections or a VERTICAL Nodes.Stack, and a Nodes.Separator only in an INLINE or ACTIONS stack, between two other children;
    • selected and expanded ids name existing items, rows or options, and expanded ids name branches;
    • a table row's cells and cell nodes name the table's columns;
    • tree item ids are unique in their tree, items nest at most 128 levels below a root item, and a tree with columns has at most one trailing value per column after the first;
    • an EXCLUSIVE Nodes.Choice has two to four options and a TABS choice at least two;
    • a Nodes.Field's listId, when not blank, names an Nodes.ItemList in the same view.
    Components
    Nodes.Noderootthe view's top node; not a Notice or a Separator

A tab is saved only while its plugin has a restorer for its kind; a saved tab whose plugin is missing or disabled, or has no restorer for its kind any more, comes back as a placeholder that says why.

    since 0.21.0

    Registers a split item (tabs and panes spec 8 and 11). Jasper lists it in every Split list (the Tab menu's and the right-click menus' Split submenus) after the terminal, the bundled plugins' items first and each in the order they registered, and registers its SplitItemSpec.rightAction() and SplitItemSpec.downAction(), which can be bound under [keybindings] and placed in the plugin's menus and toolbar as its own actions. Running one calls opener on the UI thread with the window it ran in and TabPlacement.SPLIT_RIGHT or TabPlacement.SPLIT_DOWN; the plugin opens its view there, usually with openTab(ContentSpec, WindowOwner, UiView, TabPlacement). A failing opener is contained. An opener runs as a user's Split request, possibly offered from another plugin's menu, so it should only open its view.

    since 0.8.5

    Registers this plugin's batch closing guard. No requested content closes unless every guard accepts. A pending decision blocks moves; failures refuse close. Runs for tab, window, quit and restart closes.

    Parameters
    guard requested subset and true for window/quit batch closing, returning its asynchronous decision

    #default Subscription onQuitting(Supplier<CompletableFuture<Boolean>> guard)

    since 0.11.0

    Registers a guard asked when the user quits or restarts Jasper, after content tabs' guards and before anything closes. Guards are asked one at a time; one whose future completes with false cancels the quit. A guard that throws, returns null or whose future fails allows the quit. The guard runs on the UI thread and may show a modal dialog before completing its future.

    It is asked on a real quit or restart only. A resident macOS Jasper answers Cmd+Q, Jasper › Quit, the Dock's Quit and a Jasper window's File › Quit by closing its windows through the content tabs' closing guards and going to the background. That does not ask this guard, and the plugin keeps running until Jasper really quits (Quit Jasper Completely, a log-out or a restart).

    Parameters
    guard returns the decision, possibly after asking the user

    the registration; closing it removes the guard

    Test kit jasper-sdk-testkit

    A headless fake of the plugin runtime for plugin unit tests: start a plugin against FakePluginHost, drive it, and assert what it registered.

    package dev.jasper.sdk.testing

    A headless, single-threaded stand-in for Jasper's plugin runtime, for plugin unit tests. The thread that calls FakePluginHost plays the UI thread: events wait in a queue until flush(), and background tasks wait until runBackground(). Kit views are the exception: FakeKit and FakeKitView need the real Swing event dispatch thread, so run a test of a plugin that builds views inside SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait.

    TypeKindSummary
    FakeClipboardclassThe clipboard every fake plugin's Platform writes to, as the application's clipboard behaves: a secret copy is cleared when its time is up (expireSecrets()) or its plugin stops, if the clipboard still holds it.
    FakeCommandCallclassA subcommand call FakePluginHost.call made: what the handler wrote, its exit code, and cancelling it as when the caller goes away.
    FakeKitclassFunctional, EDT-confined plugin kit; construct freely, then operate on the EDT.
    FakeKitViewclassFunctional descriptor/secret/event owner for plugin tests.
    FakeNotificationsclassWhat fake plugins posted and the groups declared for them, as the application's notification center holds them.
    FakePluginContextclassOne fake plugin's context.
    FakePluginHostclassA single-threaded plugin runtime for tests.
    FakePresentationsclassReady presentations for FakePluginHost.setPresentation.

    FakePluginHost

    dev.jasper.sdk.testing
    final class FakePluginHost
    implements AutoCloseable

    A single-threaded plugin runtime for tests. It follows the same rules as the application: queued ordered delivery, topic ownership, coalesced activity progress, services committed on a successful start, rollback and a closed context on failure. Appearance palettes and workspace subscriptions accept the creating test thread or the real Swing EDT, rejecting background workers. Kit views are the exception: FakeKit and FakeKitView need the real Swing event dispatch thread, so run a test of a plugin that builds views inside SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait.

    Constructors

    A host whose plugins' data directories live in a temporary directory this host deletes on close.

    since 0.18.3

    Queues saved terminal typography for publication on the next flush(), as a saved change to Jasper's terminal font settings would. Until then every plugin reads Jasper's defaults: Cousine Nerd Font Mono at 12 points, falling back to Symbols Nerd Font Mono and Apple Color Emoji, with ligatures and a line height of 1. The flush updates the getter first and then runs the handlers on the EDT; a value equal to the current one notifies nobody, and a handler that throws is recorded in failures() without stopping the others.

    #Optional<UUID> restoreTab(
        String pluginId,
        UUID windowId,
        String title,
        RestoreState state)

    since 0.21.0

    Restores one saved tab as Jasper does when it restores its windows (workspace tabs spec 13): the plugin's restorer for state's kind runs, and the first content tab it opens, whatever window or placement it named, or the first provided session it opens in window windowId, is the saved tab, in that window, where it stays while the restorer runs: a move asked of it does nothing. A content tab is placed there, not shown: it is neither selected nor active until the test shows it. A session's tab waits as Jasper's does, NOT_STARTED with no connection attempt, until its tab is shown (focusTerminalPane or its TabHandle.select()). Jasper places the tab where it was saved, in its tab and pane; this fake puts it in a new tab at the end of the window's strip. Call it on the UI thread.

    Parameters
    pluginId the plugin that saved the tab
    windowId the window being restored
    title the tab's saved title
    state its saved restore state
    Returns

    since 0.17.1

A name outside [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, TERM, COLORTERM, TERM_PROGRAM, TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION, a name starting JASPER_, a null value and a value holding NUL are dropped, and the first contributor of a name wins.

    Opens a document in a new tab of the window the request came from, or of the main window when owner is null; a document whose key is already open is selected in its tab, wherever that is. The interface default ignores owner.

    Parameters

    owner the Jasper window or content tab the request came from, or null
    #default Subscription reopener(
        String keyPrefix,
        Function<String, Optional<Function<WindowOwner, EditorDocument>>> resolve)

    Makes recent files under a key prefix reopenable. The resolver runs on the UI thread and must do no I/O. It returns empty when the key cannot be reopened now, for example because its host was deleted, and otherwise a factory that builds the document for the window reopening it (null when there is none). A later registration of the same prefix replaces the earlier one; the longest matching prefix wins. A resolver that throws or answers null cannot reopen the key.

    Parameters
    keyPrefix the start of the keys this plugin's documents use, for example "remote:"; not blank and not starting with "local:", which the Editor keeps for local files (IllegalArgumentException otherwise)
    resolve resolves a recorded key
    Returns
    removes the reopener
    #default Subscription opener(Predicate<OpenRequest> handler)

    Lets a plugin answer Open in Editor… in its own way, for example by browsing a remote host. Handlers run on the UI thread in registration order before the local file chooser; the first to return true has handled the request. A handler that throws counts as false.

    Parameters
    handler answers a request; true when it handled it
    Returns
    removes the handler
    #default Subscription locationDocuments(
        String sourceId,
        LocationResolver resolver)

    Lets Open in Editor… and Save As offer a file source's places and open or save what the user picks there. The chooser offers the source's roots only while a resolver is registered; a later registration for the same source replaces the earlier one.

    Parameters
    sourceId the id of a file source the plugin registered; not blank (IllegalArgumentException otherwise)
    resolver builds documents for the source's files
    Returns
    removes the resolver

    EditorDocument

    dev.jasper.editor.api
    interface EditorDocument

    A file the editor reads and writes through whoever provides it. The editor calls these methods on the UI thread; none may block. Futures may complete on any thread.

    Methods
    #String key()

    The document's stable identity. Opening a document whose key is already open selects that tab; Recent Files records the key, and Editor.reopener resolves it by its prefix. Start it with a prefix of the plugin's own, the one it passes to Editor.reopener (for example "remote:"), never "local:", which the Editor uses for local files.

    Returns
    stable identity: two documents with equal keys are the same file
    #String name()

    The file name: the tab title and the name in Recent Files and prompts. With the first line of the text, it decides the syntax highlighting.

    Returns
    the file name, used as the tab title
    #String location()

    Where the file is, in full: shown in tooltips, the status line and Recent Files. For a document with a host, the status line shows only the part from the first :/ on, without the colon.

    Returns
    the full location for tooltips and the status line, for example dustin@prod-web:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
    #Optional<String> host()

    The host a remote document lives on. A document with a host gets the server icon on its tab, a host tag in Recent Files and the host's name in its loading text and in the window title.

    Returns
    the host a remote document lives on, shown dimmed after the name; empty for a local document
    #default Optional<EditorDocument> resolveRelative(String path)

    Resolves a resource against this file's parent, retaining this handle's storage and authentication context. Called on the UI thread; performs no I/O and does not open a tab. Since Editor 0.11.0.

    Parameters
    path a nonempty, already decoded relative path with / separators; dot segments are allowed
    Returns
    the resource handle, or empty when this provider has no relative resolution support
    Throws
    IllegalArgumentException when RelativePaths.requireValid(String) rejects the path
    #CompletableFuture<Content> read(long limitBytes)

    Reads the whole file. Fails with TooLargeException, before transferring content, when it is larger than limitBytes. Cancelling the future aborts the transfer. The Editor words a TooLargeException, NoSuchFileException or AccessDeniedException itself and shows any other failure's message.

    Parameters
    limitBytes the largest size the editor accepts: its max_file_mib setting, in bytes
    Returns
    the content and the revision it was read at
    #default CompletableFuture<Content> readQuietly(long limitBytes)

    Reads the whole file as read does, for a restore, which asks the user nothing. The Editor reads a document this way when Jasper has restored its tab and the tab is first active or Load is pressed; Retry then reads it with read. A document whose read can ask the user anything (a sign-in, a prompt) must override this so that it fails, saying why, instead of asking. The default reads as read does.

    Parameters
    limitBytes the largest size the editor accepts
    Returns
    the content and the revision it was read at
    #CompletableFuture<Optional<Revision>> revision()

    The file's current revision, which the Editor asks for before each Save (not Save As). When it differs from the revision last read or written, the user chooses whether to overwrite or reload; when the file no longer exists, whether to save anyway.

    Returns
    the file's current revision, or empty when it no longer exists
    #CompletableFuture<Revision> write(byte[] content)

    Replaces the file's content: resolve symbolic links to the file they name; write a hidden sibling, give it the target's permissions and atomically replace the target; write in place instead when the sibling cannot be created, would change the owner or group, when the target has more than one hard link, or when an atomic replacement is unavailable; create a missing target; then stat it.

    Parameters
    content the new bytes; the receiver may keep the array
    Returns
    the new revision
